1.98.m: of great austerities, of prolonged austerities, most gross, aged, firm, / the day, the year, pervasiveness, standard of measurement, supreme austerity,

1.98.s:
saṃvatsarakaro mantraḥ pratyayaḥ sarvadarśanaḥ
ajaḥ sarveśvaraḥ snigdho mahāretā mahābalaḥ //
1.98.d:
संवत्सरकरो मन्त्रः प्रत्ययः सर्वदर्शनः
अजः सर्वेश्वरः स्निग्धो महारेता महाबलः ॥
1.98.m: maker of the year, mantra, conviction, seeing all, / unborn, lord of all, affectionate, of mighty seed, of great strength,

1.98.s:
yogī yogyo mahāretāḥ siddhaḥ sarvādir agnidaḥ
vasurvasumanāḥ satyaḥ sarvapāpaharo haraḥ //
1.98.d:
योगी योग्यो महारेताः सिद्धः सर्वादिर् अग्निदः
वसुर्वसुमनाः सत्यः सर्वपापहरो हरः ॥
1.98.m: the yogin, suitable, of mighty seed, perfected, beginning of all, giver of fire, / Vasu, possessing a noble mind, truth, remover of all sins, Hara,

1.98.s:
amṛtaḥ śāśvataḥ śānto bāṇahastaḥ pratāpavān
kamaṇḍaludharo dhanvī vedāṅgo vedavinmuniḥ //
1.98.d:
अमृतः शाश्वतः शान्तो बाणहस्तः प्रतापवान्
कमण्डलुधरो धन्वी वेदाङ्गो वेदविन्मुनिः ॥
1.98.m: immortal, eternal, tranquil, arrow in hand, possessing ardour, / holding a water-pot, bowman, limb of the Veda, sage knowing the Veda,

1.98.s:
bhrājiṣṇur bhojanaṃ bhoktā lokanetā durādharaḥ
atīndriyo mahāmāyaḥ sarvāvāsaścatuṣpathaḥ //
1.98.d:
भ्राजिष्णुर् भोजनं भोक्ता लोकनेता दुराधरः
अतीन्द्रियो महामायः सर्वावासश्चतुष्पथः ॥
1.98.m: radiant, food, eater, leader of the worlds, hard to restrain, / beyond the senses, of great illusion, abode of all, the crossroads,

1.98.s:
kālayogī mahānādo mahotsāho mahābalaḥ
mahābuddhir mahāvīryo bhūtacārī purandaraḥ //
1.98.d:
कालयोगी महानादो महोत्साहो महाबलः
महाबुद्धिर् महावीर्यो भूतचारी पुरन्दरः ॥
1.98.m: time-yogin, of mighty sound, of great zeal, of great strength, / of great intellect, of great virility, roamer with spirits, Purandara,

1.98.s:
niśācaraḥ pretacārī mahāśaktir mahādyutiḥ
anirdeśyavapuḥ śrīmān sarvahāryamito gatiḥ //
1.98.d:
निशाचरः प्रेतचारी महाशक्तिर् महाद्युतिः
अनिर्देश्यवपुः श्रीमान् सर्वहार्यमितो गतिः ॥
1.98.m: night-wanderer, roamer among ghosts, of great power, of great splendour, / of indescribable form, glorious, all-carrying, immeasurable, the destination,

1.98.s:
bahuśruto bahumayo niyatātmā bhavodbhavaḥ
ojastejo dyutikaro nartakaḥ sarvakāmakaḥ //
1.98.d:
बहुश्रुतो बहुमयो नियतात्मा भवोद्भवः
ओजस्तेजो द्युतिकरो नर्तकः सर्वकामकः ॥
1.98.m: learned, manifold, self-restrained, born of Bhava, / producer of vitality, energy, and lustre, dancer, fulfilling all desires,

1.98.s:
nṛtyapriyo nṛtyanṛtyaḥ prakāśātmā pratāpanaḥ
buddhaspaṣṭākṣaro mantraḥ sanmānaḥ sārasaṃplavaḥ //
1.98.d:
नृत्यप्रियो नृत्यनृत्यः प्रकाशात्मा प्रतापनः
बुद्धस्पष्टाक्षरो मन्त्रः सन्मानः सारसंप्लवः ॥
1.98.m: fond of dance, the dance of dancers, luminous in essence, burning, / the mantra with clear and revealed syllables, true honour, overflowing essence,

1.98.s:
yugādikṛd yugāvarto gaṃbhīro vṛṣavāhanaḥ
iṣṭo viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ śarabhaḥ śarabho dhanuḥ //
1.98.d:
युगादिकृद् युगावर्तो गंभीरो वृषवाहनः
इष्टो विशिष्टः शिष्टेष्टः शरभः शरभो धनुः ॥
1.98.m: maker of the yuga's beginning, turner of the yuga, profound, bull-riding, / desired, distinguished, dear to the virtuous, the Śarabha beast, the Śarabha, the bow,

1.98.s:
apāṃ nidhiradhiṣṭhānaṃ vijayo jayakālavit
pratiṣṭhitaḥ pramāṇajño hiraṇyakavaco hariḥ //
1.98.d:
अपां निधिरधिष्ठानं विजयो जयकालवित्
प्रतिष्ठितः प्रमाणज्ञो हिरण्यकवचो हरिः ॥
1.98.m: receptacle of waters, foundation, victory, knower of the time to conquer, / established, knower of means of valid knowledge, wearing golden armour, Hari,

1.98.s:
virocanaḥ suragaṇo vidyeśo vibudhāśrayaḥ
bālarūpo balonmāthī vivarto gahano guruḥ //
1.98.d:
विरोचनः सुरगणो विद्येशो विबुधाश्रयः
बालरूपो बलोन्माथी विवर्तो गहनो गुरुः ॥
1.98.m: the illuminator, host of gods, lord of lore, refuge of the wise, / having the form of a child, crusher of the strong, transformation, deep, heavy,

1.98.s:
karaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kartā sarvabandhavimocanaḥ
vidvattamo vītabhayo viśvabhartā niśākaraḥ //
1.98.d:
करणं कारणं कर्ता सर्वबन्धविमोचनः
विद्वत्तमो वीतभयो विश्वभर्ता निशाकरः ॥
1.98.m: the instrument, the cause, the agent, liberator from all bonds, / most wise, free from fear, sustainer of the universe, maker of night,

1.98.s:
vyavasāyo vyavasthānaḥ sthānado jagadādijaḥ
dundubho lalito viśvo bhavātmātmani saṃsthitaḥ //
1.98.d:
व्यवसायो व्यवस्थानः स्थानदो जगदादिजः
दुन्दुभो ललितो विश्वो भवात्मात्मनि संस्थितः ॥
1.98.m: resolve, established order, giver of station, born first of the universe, / the drum, charming, the universe, identical with Bhava, abiding in the Self,

1.98.s:
vīreśvaro vīrabhadro vīrahā vīrabhṛd virāṭ
vīracūḍāmaṇirvettā tīvranādo nadīdharaḥ //
1.98.d:
वीरेश्वरो वीरभद्रो वीरहा वीरभृद् विराट्
वीरचूडामणिर्वेत्ता तीव्रनादो नदीधरः ॥
1.98.m: lord of heroes, Vīrabhadra, slayer of heroes, supporter of heroes, sovereign ruler, / crest-jewel of heroes, knower, of sharp sound, bearer of the river,

1.98.s:
ājñādharastriśūlī ca śipiviṣṭaḥ śivālayaḥ
vālakhilyo mahācāpas tigmāṃśur nidhir avyayaḥ //
1.98.d:
आज्ञाधरस्त्रिशूली च शिपिविष्टः शिवालयः
वालखिल्यो महाचापस् तिग्मांशुर् निधिर् अव्ययः ॥
1.98.m: bearer of commands, trident-bearer, Sipiviṣṭa, abode of Śiva, / the Vālakhilya, possessor of the great bow, hot-rayed, imperishable treasure,

1.98.s:
abhirāmaḥ suśaraṇaḥ subrahmaṇyaḥ sudhāpatiḥ
maghavānkauśiko gomān viśrāmaḥ sarvaśāsanaḥ //
1.98.d:
अभिरामः सुशरणः सुब्रह्मण्यः सुधापतिः
मघवान्कौशिको गोमान् विश्रामः सर्वशासनः ॥
1.98.m: delightful, good refuge, Subrahmaṇya, lord of nectar, / Maghavan, Kauśika, rich in cattle, resting place, ruler of all,

1.98.s:
lalāṭākṣo viśvadehaḥ sāraḥ saṃsāracakrabhṛt
amoghadaṇḍī madhyastho hiraṇyo brahmavarcasī //
1.98.d:
ललाटाक्षो विश्वदेहः सारः संसारचक्रभृत्
अमोघदण्डी मध्यस्थो हिरण्यो ब्रह्मवर्चसी ॥
1.98.m: with an eye on the forehead, having the universe as body, the essence, bearer of the wheel of saṃsāra, / of unerring punishment, impartial, golden, radiant with sacred lustre,

1.98.s:
paramārthaḥ paramayaḥ śambaro vyāghrako 'nalaḥ
rucir vararucir vandyo vācaspatiraharpatiḥ //
1.98.d:
परमार्थः परमयः शम्बरो व्याघ्रको ऽनलः
रुचिर् वररुचिर् वन्द्यो वाचस्पतिरहर्पतिः ॥
1.98.m: supreme reality, consisting of the highest, Śambara, the tiger, fire, / brightness, exquisite light, worthy of praise, lord of speech, lord of the day,

1.98.s:
ravirvirocanaḥ skandhaḥ śāstā vaivasvato janaḥ
yuktirunnatakīrtiś ca śāntarāgaḥ parājayaḥ //
1.98.d:
रविर्विरोचनः स्कन्धः शास्ता वैवस्वतो जनः
युक्तिरुन्नतकीर्तिश् च शान्तरागः पराजयः ॥
1.98.m: the sun, Virocana, the trunk, ruler, Vaivasvata, mankind, / expedient, of exalted fame, free from passion, defeat,

1.98.s:
kailāsapatikāmāriḥ savitā ravilocanaḥ
vidvattamo vītabhayo viśvahartā nivāritaḥ //
1.98.d:
कैलासपतिकामारिः सविता रविलोचनः
विद्वत्तमो वीतभयो विश्वहर्ता निवारितः ॥
1.98.m: lord of Kailāsa, enemy of Kāma, the generator, sun-eyed, / most wise, free from fear, destroyer of the universe, unrestrained,

1.98.s:
nityo niyatakalyāṇaḥ puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ
dūraśravā viśvasaho dhyeyo duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ //
1.98.d:
नित्यो नियतकल्याणः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः
दूरश्रवा विश्वसहो ध्येयो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः ॥
1.98.m: eternal, constant in auspiciousness, whose hearing and praise yield merit, / heard from afar, enduring all, to be meditated upon, destroyer of bad dreams,

1.98.s:
uttārako duṣkṛtihā durdharṣo duḥsaho 'bhayaḥ
anādirbhūrbhuvolakṣmīḥ kirīṭī tridaśādhipaḥ //
1.98.d:
उत्तारको दुष्कृतिहा दुर्धर्षो दुःसहो ऽभयः
अनादिर्भूर्भुवोलक्ष्मीः किरीटी त्रिदशाधिपः ॥
1.98.m: saviour, destroyer of evil deeds, unassailable, hard to bear, fearless, / beginningless, earth, atmosphere, fortune, diademed, sovereign of the thirty gods,

1.98.s:
viśvagoptā viśvabhartā sudhīro rucirāṅgadaḥ
janano janajanmādiḥ prītimānnītimānnayaḥ //
1.98.d:
विश्वगोप्ता विश्वभर्ता सुधीरो रुचिराङ्गदः
जननो जनजन्मादिः प्रीतिमान्नीतिमान्नयः ॥
1.98.m: protector of the universe, sustainer of the universe, very steadfast, wearing splendid armlets, / source, origin of the birth of creatures, affectionate, moral, policy,

1.98.s:
viśiṣṭaḥ kāśyapo bhānur bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
praṇavaḥ saptadhācāro mahākāyo mahādhanuḥ //
1.98.d:
विशिष्टः काश्यपो भानुर् भीमो भीमपराक्रमः
प्रणवः सप्तधाचारो महाकायो महाधनुः ॥
1.98.m: distinguished, Kāśyapa, the sun, fierce, of fierce valour, / the Praṇava, practicing the sevenfold path, of immense body, possessor of a great bow,

1.98.s:
janmādhipo mahādevaḥ sakalāgamapāragaḥ
tattvātattvavivekātmā vibhūṣṇur bhūtibhūṣaṇaḥ //
1.98.d:
जन्माधिपो महादेवः सकलागमपारगः
तत्त्वातत्त्वविवेकात्मा विभूष्णुर् भूतिभूषणः ॥
1.98.m: lord of birth, Mahādeva, master of all scriptures, / discriminator between truth and untruth, desiring to expand, adorned with sacred ash,

1.98.s:
ṛṣirbrāhmaṇavijjiṣṇur janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ
yajño yajñapatiryajvā yajñānto 'moghavikramaḥ //
1.98.d:
ऋषिर्ब्राह्मणविज्जिष्णुर् जन्ममृत्युजरातिगः
यज्ञो यज्ञपतिर्यज्वा यज्ञान्तो ऽमोघविक्रमः ॥
1.98.m: the sage, knower of Brahmā, victorious, beyond birth, death, and old age, / sacrifice, lord of sacrifice, sacrificer, end of sacrifice, of unfailing prowess,

1.98.s:
mahendro durbharaḥ senī yajñāṅgo yajñavāhanaḥ
pañcabrahmasamutpattir viśveśo vimalodayaḥ //
1.98.d:
महेन्द्रो दुर्भरः सेनी यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञवाहनः
पञ्चब्रह्मसमुत्पत्तिर् विश्वेशो विमलोदयः ॥
1.98.m: Mahendra, hard to sustain, possessing an army, part of sacrifice, vehicle of sacrifice, / origin of the five Brahmans, lord of the universe, of spotless dawn,

1.98.s:
ātmayonir anādyantaḥ ṣaḍviṃśatsaptalokadhṛk
gāyatrīvallabhaḥ prāṃśur viśvāvāsaḥ prabhākaraḥ //
1.98.d:
आत्मयोनिर् अनाद्यन्तः षड्विंशत्सप्तलोकधृक्
गायत्रीवल्लभः प्रांशुर् विश्वावासः प्रभाकरः ॥
1.98.m: self-born, without beginning or end, the twenty-sixth principle, supporter of the seven worlds, / beloved of the Gāyatrī, tall, abode of the universe, maker of light,

1.98.s:
śiśurgirirataḥ samrāṭ suṣeṇaḥ suraśatruhā
amogho 'riṣṭamathano mukundo vigatajvaraḥ //
1.98.d:
शिशुर्गिरिरतः सम्राट् सुषेणः सुरशत्रुहा
अमोघो ऽरिष्टमथनो मुकुन्दो विगतज्वरः ॥
1.98.m: the child, delighting in mountains, sovereign, having good armies, slayer of the enemies of the gods, / unfailing, crusher of misfortune, Mukunda, freed from distress,

1.98.s:
svayaṃjyotir anujyotir ātmajyotir acañcalaḥ
piṅgalaḥ kapilaśmaśruḥ śāstranetras trayītanuḥ //
1.98.d:
स्वयंज्योतिर् अनुज्योतिर् आत्मज्योतिर् अचञ्चलः
पिङ्गलः कपिलश्मश्रुः शास्त्रनेत्रस् त्रयीतनुः ॥
1.98.m: self-luminous, secondary light, light of the Self, unwavering, / tawny, having a reddish-brown beard, having the scriptures as eyes, having the threefold Veda as body,

1.98.s:
jñānaskandho mahājñānī nirutpattir upaplavaḥ
bhago vivasvānādityo yogācāryo bṛhaspatiḥ //
1.98.d:
ज्ञानस्कन्धो महाज्ञानी निरुत्पत्तिर् उपप्लवः
भगो विवस्वानादित्यो योगाचार्यो बृहस्पतिः ॥
1.98.m: aggregate of knowledge, possessed of great wisdom, devoid of origination, calamity, / Bhaga, Vivasvat, Āditya, master of yoga, Bṛhaspati,

1.98.s:
udārakīrtir udyogī sadyogī sadasanmayaḥ
nakṣatramālī rākeśaḥ sādhiṣṭhānaḥ ṣaḍāśrayaḥ //
1.98.d:
उदारकीर्तिर् उद्योगी सद्योगी सदसन्मयः
नक्षत्रमाली राकेशः साधिष्ठानः षडाश्रयः ॥
1.98.m: of exalted fame, energetic, true yogin, composed of existence and non-existence, / garlanded with constellations, lord of the full moon, possessing a base, six-supported,

1.98.s:
pavitrapāṇiḥ pāpārir maṇipūro manogatiḥ
hṛtpuṇḍarīkamāsīnaḥ śuklaḥ śānto vṛṣākapiḥ //
1.98.d:
पवित्रपाणिः पापारिर् मणिपूरो मनोगतिः
हृत्पुण्डरीकमासीनः शुक्लः शान्तो वृषाकपिः ॥
1.98.m: pure-handed, foe of sin, Maṇipūra, swift as thought, / seated on the lotus of the heart, white, tranquil, Vṛṣākapi,

1.98.s:
viṣṇurgrahapatiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ samartho 'narthanāśanaḥ
adharmaśatrurakṣayyaḥ puruhūtaḥ puruṣṭutaḥ //
1.98.d:
विष्णुर्ग्रहपतिः कृष्णः समर्थो ऽनर्थनाशनः
अधर्मशत्रुरक्षय्यः पुरुहूतः पुरुष्टुतः ॥
1.98.m: Viṣṇu, lord of the planets, Kṛṣṇa, capable, destroyer of misfortune, / enemy of unrighteousness, imperishable, invoked by many, praised by many,

1.98.s:
brahmagarbho bṛhadgarbho dharmadhenurdhanāgamaḥ
jagaddhitaiṣī sugataḥ kumāraḥ kuśalāgamaḥ //
1.98.d:
ब्रह्मगर्भो बृहद्गर्भो धर्मधेनुर्धनागमः
जगद्धितैषी सुगतः कुमारः कुशलागमः ॥
1.98.m: womb of Brahman, great womb, cow of righteousness, arrival of wealth, / wishing the welfare of the world, Sugata, youth, attainment of prosperity,

1.98.s:
hiraṇyavarṇo jyotiṣmān nānābhūtadharo dhvaniḥ
arogo niyamādhyakṣo viśvāmitro dvijottamaḥ //
1.98.d:
हिरण्यवर्णो ज्योतिष्मान् नानाभूतधरो ध्वनिः
अरोगो नियमाध्यक्षो विश्वामित्रो द्विजोत्तमः ॥
1.98.m: golden-hued, luminous, bearer of diverse beings, sound, / free from disease, overseer of rules, Viśvāmitra, foremost among the twice-born,

1.98.s:
bṛhajjyotiḥ sudhāmā ca mahājyotiranuttamaḥ
mātāmaho mātariśvā nabhasvān nāgahāradhṛk //
1.98.d:
बृहज्ज्योतिः सुधामा च महाज्योतिरनुत्तमः
मातामहो मातरिश्वा नभस्वान् नागहारधृक् ॥
1.98.m: great light, of lovely dwelling, supreme light, having no superior, / maternal grandfather, wind, atmosphere, wearing a garland of serpents,

1.98.s:
pulastyaḥ pulaho 'gastyo jātūkarṇyaḥ parāśaraḥ
nirāvaraṇadharmajño viriñco viṣṭaraśravāḥ //
1.98.d:
पुलस्त्यः पुलहो ऽगस्त्यो जातूकर्ण्यः पराशरः
निरावरणधर्मज्ञो विरिञ्चो विष्टरश्रवाः ॥
1.98.m: Pulastya, Pulaha, Agastya, Jātūkarṇya, Parāśara, / knower of unveiled dharma, Viriñca, Viṣṭaraśravas,

1.98.s:
ātmabhūr aniruddho 'trijñānamūrtir mahāyaśāḥ
lokacūḍāmaṇirvīraḥ caṇḍasatyaparākramaḥ //
1.98.d:
आत्मभूर् अनिरुद्धो ऽत्रिज्ञानमूर्तिर् महायशाः
लोकचूडामणिर्वीरः चण्डसत्यपराक्रमः ॥
1.98.m: self-existent, Aniruddha, Atri, embodiment of knowledge, of great renown, / crest-jewel of the worlds, hero, fierce, of true valour,

1.98.s:
vyālakalpo mahākalpo mahāvṛkṣaḥ kalādharaḥ
alaṃkariṣṇus tvacalo rociṣṇurvikramottamaḥ //
1.98.d:
व्यालकल्पो महाकल्पो महावृक्षः कलाधरः
अलंकरिष्णुस् त्वचलो रोचिष्णुर्विक्रमोत्तमः ॥
1.98.m: like a serpent, great kalpa, great tree, possessor of digits, / eager to adorn, immovable, radiant, supreme in prowess,

1.98.s:
āśuśabdapatirvegī plavanaḥ śikhisārathiḥ
asaṃsṛṣṭo 'tithiḥ śakraḥ pramāthī pāpanāśanaḥ //
1.98.d:
आशुशब्दपतिर्वेगी प्लवनः शिखिसारथिः
असंसृष्टो ऽतिथिः शक्रः प्रमाथी पापनाशनः ॥
1.98.m: lord of rapid sound, swift, leaping, having fire as charioteer, / unattached, guest, Śakra, harasser, destroyer of sins,

1.98.s:
vasuśravāḥ kavyavāhaḥ pratapto viśvabhojanaḥ
jaryo jarādhiśamano lohitaś ca tanūnapāt //
1.98.d:
वसुश्रवाः कव्यवाहः प्रतप्तो विश्वभोजनः
जर्यो जराधिशमनो लोहितश् च तनूनपात् ॥
1.98.m: of rich fame, conveyer of oblations to the ancestors, burning, consumer of all, / worthy of praise, dispeller of old age and anguish, red, fire,

1.98.s:
pṛṣadaśvo nabhoyoniḥ supratīkas tamisrahā
nidāghastapano meghaḥ pakṣaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ //
1.98.d:
पृषदश्वो नभोयोनिः सुप्रतीकस् तमिस्रहा
निदाघस्तपनो मेघः पक्षः परपुरंजयः ॥
1.98.m: having dappled horses, whose source is the sky, of pleasant face, destroyer of darkness, / heat, the sun, cloud, lunar fortnight, conqueror of enemies' cities,

1.98.s:
mukhānilaḥ suniṣpannaḥ surabhiḥ śiśirātmakaḥ
vasaṃto mādhavo grīṣmo nabhasyo bījavāhanaḥ //
1.98.d:
मुखानिलः सुनिष्पन्नः सुरभिः शिशिरात्मकः
वसंतो माधवो ग्रीष्मो नभस्यो बीजवाहनः ॥
1.98.m: breath of the mouth, well-accomplished, fragrant, cold-seasoned, / spring, Mādhava, summer, the rainy season, conveyor of seeds,

1.98.s:
aṅgirā munirātreyo vimalo viśvavāhanaḥ
pāvanaḥ purujicchakras trividyo naravāhanaḥ //
1.98.d:
अङ्गिरा मुनिरात्रेयो विमलो विश्ववाहनः
पावनः पुरुजिच्छक्रस् त्रिविद्यो नरवाहनः ॥
1.98.m: Aṅgiras, the sage Ātreya, pure, bearer of all, / purifier, conqueror of many, Śakra, having threefold knowledge, riding men,

1.98.s:
mano buddhirahaṅkāraḥ kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetrapālakaḥ
tejonidhir jñānanidhir vipāko vighnakārakaḥ //
1.98.d:
मनो बुद्धिरहङ्कारः क्षेत्रज्ञः क्षेत्रपालकः
तेजोनिधिर् ज्ञाननिधिर् विपाको विघ्नकारकः ॥
1.98.m: mind, intellect, egoity, knower of the field, protector of the field, / treasury of splendour, treasury of knowledge, ripening, causer of obstacles,

1.98.s:
adharo 'nuttaro jñeyo jyeṣṭho niḥśreyasālayaḥ
śailo nagastanurdeho dānavārirarindamaḥ //
1.98.d:
अधरो ऽनुत्तरो ज्ञेयो ज्येष्ठो निःश्रेयसालयः
शैलो नगस्तनुर्देहो दानवारिररिन्दमः ॥
1.98.m: unsupported, unsurpassed, to be known, eldest, abode of liberation, / rock, mountain, form, body, foe of the Dānavas, subduer of enemies,

1.98.s:
cārudhīr janakaścāruviśalyo lokaśalyakṛt
caturvedaścaturbhāvaś caturaścaturapriyaḥ //
1.98.d:
चारुधीर् जनकश्चारुविशल्यो लोकशल्यकृत्
चतुर्वेदश्चतुर्भावश् चतुरश्चतुरप्रियः ॥
1.98.m: of pleasant mind, progenitor, lovely, free from darts, inflicter of darts upon the world, / the four Vedas, of fourfold nature, clever, fond of the clever.

1.98.s:
āmnāyo 'tha samāmnāyas tīrthadevaśivālayaḥ
bahurūpo mahārūpaḥ sarvarūpaś carācaraḥ //
1.98.d:
आम्नायो ऽथ समाम्नायस् तीर्थदेवशिवालयः
बहुरूपो महारूपः सर्वरूपश् चराचरः ॥
1.98.m: Sacred tradition and the collection of tradition, the shrine of holy waters and gods, / multiform, of great form, of all forms, moving and unmoving;

1.98.s:
nyāyanirvāhako nyāyo nyāyagamyo nirañjanaḥ
sahasramūrdhā devendraḥ sarvaśastraprabhañjanaḥ //
1.98.d:
न्यायनिर्वाहको न्यायो न्यायगम्यो निरञ्जनः
सहस्रमूर्धा देवेन्द्रः सर्वशस्त्रप्रभञ्जनः ॥
1.98.m: the administrator of justice, justice itself, reachable through justice, stainless, / thousand-headed, lord of gods, crusher of all weapons;

1.98.s:
muṇḍo virūpo vikṛto daṇḍī dānto guṇottamaḥ
piṅgalākṣo 'tha haryakṣo nīlagrīvo nirāmayaḥ //
1.98.d:
मुण्डो विरूपो विकृतो दण्डी दान्तो गुणोत्तमः
पिङ्गलाक्षो ऽथ हर्यक्षो नीलग्रीवो निरामयः ॥
1.98.m: shaven-headed, misshapen, altered, staff-bearing, self-controlled, best in virtues, / tawny-eyed and lion-eyed, blue-throated, free from disease;

1.98.s:
sahasrabāhuḥ sarveśaḥ śaraṇyaḥ sarvalokabhṛt
padmāsanaḥ paraṃ jyotiḥ parāvaraṃ paraṃ phalam //
1.98.d:
सहस्रबाहुः सर्वेशः शरण्यः सर्वलोकभृत्
पद्मासनः परं ज्योतिः परावरं परं फलम् ॥
1.98.m: thousand-armed, lord of all, refuge, bearer of all worlds, / seated on a lotus, supreme light, the higher and the lower, the supreme fruit;

1.98.s:
padmagarbho mahāgarbho viśvagarbho vicakṣaṇaḥ
parāvarajño bījeśaḥ sumukhaḥ sumahāsvanaḥ //
1.98.d:
पद्मगर्भो महागर्भो विश्वगर्भो विचक्षणः
परावरज्ञो बीजेशः सुमुखः सुमहास्वनः ॥
1.98.m: having a lotus womb, having a great womb, having the universe in his womb, discerning, / knower of the higher and lower, lord of the seed, handsome-faced, of exceedingly great sound;

1.98.s:
devāsuragururdevo devāsuranamaskṛtaḥ
devāsuramahāmātro devāsuramahāśrayaḥ //
1.98.d:
देवासुरगुरुर्देवो देवासुरनमस्कृतः
देवासुरमहामात्रो देवासुरमहाश्रयः ॥
1.98.m: teacher of gods and asuras, the god bowed to by gods and asuras, / great minister of gods and asuras, great refuge of gods and asuras;

1.98.s:
devādidevo devarṣidevāsuravarapradaḥ
devāsureśvaro divyo devāsuramaheśvaraḥ //
1.98.d:
देवादिदेवो देवर्षिदेवासुरवरप्रदः
देवासुरेश्वरो दिव्यो देवासुरमहेश्वरः ॥
1.98.m: primeval god of gods, boon-giver to divine sages, gods, and asuras, / lord of gods and asuras, divine, Maheśvara of gods and asuras;

1.98.s:
sarvadevamayo 'cintyo devatātmātmasaṃbhavaḥ
īḍyo 'nīśaḥ suravyāghro devasiṃho divākaraḥ //
1.98.d:
सर्वदेवमयो ऽचिन्त्यो देवतात्मात्मसंभवः
ईड्यो ऽनीशः सुरव्याघ्रो देवसिंहो दिवाकरः ॥
1.98.m: consisting of all gods, inconceivable, self of deities, self-born, / praiseworthy, having no master, tiger among gods, lion among gods, maker of day;

1.98.s:
vibudhāgravaraśreṣṭhaḥ sarvadevottamottamaḥ
śivajñānarataḥ śrīmān śikhiśrīparvatapriyaḥ //
1.98.d:
विबुधाग्रवरश्रेष्ठः सर्वदेवोत्तमोत्तमः
शिवज्ञानरतः श्रीमान् शिखिश्रीपर्वतप्रियः ॥
1.98.m: foremost and best among the wise, highest of all the highest gods, / devoted to the knowledge of Śiva, glorious, fond of the Śrī mountain and Śikhin;

1.98.s:
jayastaṃbho viśiṣṭambho narasiṃhanipātanaḥ
brahmacārī lokacārī dharmacārī dhanādhipaḥ //
1.98.d:
जयस्तंभो विशिष्टम्भो नरसिंहनिपातनः
ब्रह्मचारी लोकचारी धर्मचारी धनाधिपः ॥
1.98.m: pillar of victory, possessing distinct pillars, feller of the man-lion, / student of Brahman, moving through the worlds, walker in righteousness, lord of wealth;

1.98.s:
nandī nandīśvaro nagno nagnavratadharaḥ śuciḥ
liṅgādhyakṣaḥ surādhyakṣo yugādhyakṣo yugāvahaḥ //
1.98.d:
नन्दी नन्दीश्वरो नग्नो नग्नव्रतधरः शुचिः
लिङ्गाध्यक्षः सुराध्यक्षो युगाध्यक्षो युगावहः ॥
1.98.m: joyful, lord of joy, naked, observing the vow of nakedness, pure, / presiding deity of the liṅga, presiding deity of the gods, presiding deity of the yugas, bringer of the yugas;

1.98.s:
svavaśaḥ savaśaḥ svargaḥ svaraḥ svaramayasvanaḥ
bījādhyakṣo bījakartā dhanakṛd dharmavardhanaḥ //
1.98.d:
स्ववशः सवशः स्वर्गः स्वरः स्वरमयस्वनः
बीजाध्यक्षो बीजकर्ता धनकृद् धर्मवर्धनः ॥
1.98.m: self-controlled, commanding others, heaven, sound, sound consisting of notes, / overseer of the seed, maker of the seed, creator of wealth, increaser of righteousness;

1.98.s:
daṃbho 'dambho mahādaṃbhaḥ sarvabhūtamaheśvaraḥ
śmaśānanilayastiṣyaḥ seturapratimākṛtiḥ //
1.98.d:
दंभो ऽदम्भो महादंभः सर्वभूतमहेश्वरः
श्मशाननिलयस्तिष्यः सेतुरप्रतिमाकृतिः ॥
1.98.m: arrogance, free from deceit, great ostentation, Maheśvara of all beings, / dwelling in the cremation ground, Tiṣya, the bridge, of incomparable form;

1.98.s:
lokottarasphuṭālokas tryaṃbako nāgabhūṣaṇaḥ
andhakārirmakhadveṣī viṣṇukandharapātanaḥ //
1.98.d:
लोकोत्तरस्फुटालोकस् त्र्यंबको नागभूषणः
अन्धकारिर्मखद्वेषी विष्णुकन्धरपातनः ॥
1.98.m: of extraordinary and radiant light, three-eyed, adorned with serpents, / enemy of Andhaka, hater of the sacrifice, feller of Viṣṇu’s neck;

1.98.s:
vītadoṣo 'kṣayaguṇo dakṣāriḥ pūṣadantahṛt
dhūrjaṭiḥ khaṇḍaparaśuḥ sakalo niṣkalo 'naghaḥ //
1.98.d:
वीतदोषो ऽक्षयगुणो दक्षारिः पूषदन्तहृत्
धूर्जटिः खण्डपरशुः सकलो निष्कलो ऽनघः ॥
1.98.m: free from flaws, of imperishable virtues, enemy of Dakṣa, tearer of Pūṣan's teeth, / having matted hair, wielding an axe, possessing parts, partless, sinless;

1.98.s:
ādhāraḥ sakalādhāraḥ pāṇḍurābho mṛḍo naṭaḥ
pūrṇaḥ pūrayitā puṇyaḥ sukumāraḥ sulocanaḥ //
1.98.d:
आधारः सकलाधारः पाण्डुराभो मृडो नटः
पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः सुकुमारः सुलोचनः ॥
1.98.m: support, support of all, whitish-pale, Mṛḍa, dancer, / full, fulfiller, holy, delicate, fair-eyed;

1.98.s:
sāmageyaḥ priyakaraḥ puṇyakīrtiranāmayaḥ
manojavastīrthakaro jaṭilo jīviteśvaraḥ //
1.98.d:
सामगेयः प्रियकरः पुण्यकीर्तिरनामयः
मनोजवस्तीर्थकरो जटिलो जीवितेश्वरः ॥
1.98.m: to be sung in Sāmans, doing what is pleasing, of holy renown, free from affliction, / swift as thought, maker of holy bathing places, matted-haired, lord of life;

1.98.s:
jīvitāntakaro nityo vasuretā vasupriyaḥ
sadgatiḥ satkṛtiḥ saktaḥ kālakaṇṭhaḥ kalādharaḥ //
1.98.d:
जीवितान्तकरो नित्यो वसुरेता वसुप्रियः
सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सक्तः कालकण्ठः कलाधरः ॥
1.98.m: ender of life, eternal, possessing gold-semen, lover of wealth, / path of the good, virtuous action, attached, black-necked, bearer of the crescent moon;

1.98.s:
mānī mānyo mahākālaḥ sadbhūtiḥ satparāyaṇaḥ
candrasaṃjīvanaḥ śāstā lokagūḍho 'marādhipaḥ //
1.98.d:
मानी मान्यो महाकालः सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः
चन्द्रसंजीवनः शास्ता लोकगूढो ऽमराधिपः ॥
1.98.m: proud, worthy of honor, Mahākāla, good prosperity, the refuge of the good, / reviver of the moon, ruler, hidden from the world, lord of the immortals;

1.98.s:
lokabandhurlokanāthaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtibhūṣaṇaḥ
anapāyyakṣaraḥ kāntaḥ sarvaśāstrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ //
1.98.d:
लोकबन्धुर्लोकनाथः कृतज्ञः कृतिभूषणः
अनपाय्यक्षरः कान्तः सर्वशास्त्रभृतां वरः ॥
1.98.m: friend of the world, lord of the world, grateful, adorner of deeds, / imperishable, unalterable, charming, best of all wielders of weapons;

1.98.s:
tejomayo dyutidharo lokamāyo 'graṇīr aṇuḥ
śucismitaḥ prasannātmā durjayo duratikramaḥ //
1.98.d:
तेजोमयो द्युतिधरो लोकमायो ऽग्रणीर् अणुः
शुचिस्मितः प्रसन्नात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः ॥
1.98.m: consisting of splendor, bearer of brightness, worldly illusion, leader, subtle, / pure-smiling, gracious in spirit, difficult to conquer, insurmountable;

1.98.s:
jyotirmayo nirākāro jagannātho jaleśvaraḥ
tumbavīṇī mahākāyo viśokaḥ śokanāśanaḥ //
1.98.d:
ज्योतिर्मयो निराकारो जगन्नाथो जलेश्वरः
तुम्बवीणी महाकायो विशोकः शोकनाशनः ॥
1.98.m: consisting of light, formless, lord of the universe, lord of the waters, / playing the gourd lute, having a vast body, free from sorrow, destroyer of sorrow;

1.98.s:
trilokātmā trilokeśaḥ śuddhaḥ śuddhī rathākṣajaḥ
avyaktalakṣaṇo vyakto vyaktāvyakto viśāṃpatiḥ //
1.98.d:
त्रिलोकात्मा त्रिलोकेशः शुद्धः शुद्धी रथाक्षजः
अव्यक्तलक्षणो व्यक्तो व्यक्ताव्यक्तो विशांपतिः ॥
1.98.m: self of the three worlds, lord of the three worlds, pure, purifier, born from the axle of the chariot, / unmanifest in mark, manifest, manifest and unmanifest, lord of peoples;

1.98.s:
varaśīlo varatulo māno mānadhano mayaḥ
brahmā viṣṇuḥ prajāpālo haṃso haṃsagatiryamaḥ //
1.98.d:
वरशीलो वरतुलो मानो मानधनो मयः
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः प्रजापालो हंसो हंसगतिर्यमः ॥
1.98.m: of excellent conduct, of excellent balance, standard of measure, having pride as wealth, Maya, / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, protector of subjects, haṃsa, having the gait of a swan, Yama;

1.98.s:
vedhā dhātā vidhātā ca attā hartā caturmukhaḥ
kailāsaśikharāvāsī sarvāvāsī satāṃ gatiḥ //
1.98.d:
वेधा धाता विधाता च अत्ता हर्ता चतुर्मुखः
कैलासशिखरावासी सर्वावासी सतां गतिः ॥
1.98.m: creator, Ordainer, Arranger, consumer, remover, four-faced, / dweller on Kailāsa's peak, dweller in all, refuge of the virtuous;

1.98.s:
hiraṇyagarbho hariṇaḥ puruṣaḥ pūrvajaḥ pitā
bhūtālayo bhūtapatir bhūtido bhuvaneśvaraḥ //
1.98.d:
हिरण्यगर्भो हरिणः पुरुषः पूर्वजः पिता
भूतालयो भूतपतिर् भूतिदो भुवनेश्वरः ॥
1.98.m: Hiraṇyagarbha, deer-like, Puruṣa, first-born, father, / abode of beings, lord of beings, giver of welfare, lord of the worlds;

1.98.s:
saṃyogī yogavidbrahma brahmaṇyo brāhmaṇapriyaḥ
devapriyo devanātho devajño devacintakaḥ //
1.98.d:
संयोगी योगविद्ब्रह्म ब्रह्मण्यो ब्राह्मणप्रियः
देवप्रियो देवनाथो देवज्ञो देवचिन्तकः ॥
1.98.m: in union, knower of yoga, Brahman, friendly to brāhmaṇas, fond of brāhmaṇas, / dear to the gods, lord of the gods, knower of the gods, thinking of the gods;

1.98.s:
viṣamākṣaḥ kalādhyakṣo vṛṣāṅko vṛṣavardhanaḥ
nirmado nirahaṅkāro nirmoho nirupadravaḥ //
1.98.d:
विषमाक्षः कलाध्यक्षो वृषाङ्को वृषवर्धनः
निर्मदो निरहङ्कारो निर्मोहो निरुपद्रवः ॥
1.98.m: having uneven eyes, lord of the arts, bull-marked, increaser of righteousness, / free from arrogance, free from egotism, free from delusion, free from trouble;

1.98.s:
darpahā darpito dṛptaḥ sarvartuparivartakaḥ
saptajihvaḥ sahasrārciḥ snigdhaḥ prakṛtidakṣiṇaḥ //
1.98.d:
दर्पहा दर्पितो दृप्तः सर्वर्तुपरिवर्तकः
सप्तजिह्वः सहस्रार्चिः स्निग्धः प्रकृतिदक्षिणः ॥
1.98.m: destroyer of pride, proud, haughty, revolving through all the seasons, / seven-tongued, thousand-rayed, gentle, simple by nature;

1.98.s:
bhūtabhavyabhavannāthaḥ prabhavo bhrāntināśanaḥ
artho 'nartho mahākośaḥ parakāryaikapaṇḍitaḥ //
1.98.d:
भूतभव्यभवन्नाथः प्रभवो भ्रान्तिनाशनः
अर्थो ऽनर्थो महाकोशः परकार्यैकपण्डितः ॥
1.98.m: lord of past, future, and present, origin, destroyer of error, / wealth, misfortune, great treasury, skilled solely in the affairs of others;

1.98.s:
niṣkaṇṭakaḥ kṛtānando nirvyājo vyājamardanaḥ
sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyakīrtistambhakṛtāgamaḥ //
1.98.d:
निष्कण्टकः कृतानन्दो निर्व्याजो व्याजमर्दनः
सत्त्ववान् सात्त्विकः सत्यकीर्तिस्तम्भकृतागमः ॥
1.98.m: free from thorns, having bliss made, free from guile, crusher of deceit, / endowed with sattva, sāttvika, renowned for truth, maker of pillars, tradition;

1.98.s:
akaṃpito guṇagrāhī naikātmā naikakarmakṛt
suprītaḥ sumukhaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sukaro dakṣiṇo 'nalaḥ //
1.98.d:
अकंपितो गुणग्राही नैकात्मा नैककर्मकृत्
सुप्रीतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुकरो दक्षिणो ऽनलः ॥
1.98.m: unshaken, receptive of virtues, not having a single self, performer of varied deeds, / well-pleased, fair-faced, subtle, easy to do, auspicious, Agni;

1.98.s:
skandhaḥ skandhadharo dhuryaḥ prakaṭaḥ prītivardhanaḥ
aparājitaḥ sarvasaho vidagdhaḥ sarvavāhanaḥ //
1.98.d:
स्कन्धः स्कन्धधरो धुर्यः प्रकटः प्रीतिवर्धनः
अपराजितः सर्वसहो विदग्धः सर्ववाहनः ॥
1.98.m: Skandha, bearer of the shoulder, foremost bearer of burdens, manifest, increaser of love, / invincible, all-enduring, wise, borne by all;

1.98.s:
adhṛtaḥ svadhṛtaḥ sādhyaḥ pūrvamūrtiryaśodharaḥ
varāhaśṛṅgadhṛg vāyur balavān ekanāyakaḥ //
1.98.d:
अधृतः स्वधृतः साध्यः पूर्वमूर्तिर्यशोधरः
वराहशृङ्गधृग् वायुर् बलवान् एकनायकः ॥
1.98.m: unsupported, self-supported, to be accomplished, primeval form, bearer of glory, / holding the tusk of the boar, wind, mighty, sole leader;

1.98.s:
śrutiprakāśaḥ śrutimān ekabandhur anekadhṛk
śrīvallabhaśivārambhaḥ śāntabhadraḥ samañjasaḥ //
1.98.d:
श्रुतिप्रकाशः श्रुतिमान् एकबन्धुर् अनेकधृक्
श्रीवल्लभशिवारम्भः शान्तभद्रः समञ्जसः ॥
1.98.m: illumination of revelation, master of revelation, sole friend, bearer of many, / beloved of Śrī, whose undertakings are auspicious, peaceful and gracious, proper;

1.98.s:
bhūśayo bhūtikṛdbhūtir bhūṣaṇo bhūtavāhanaḥ
akāyo bhaktakāyasthaḥ kālajñānī kalāvapuḥ //
1.98.d:
भूशयो भूतिकृद्भूतिर् भूषणो भूतवाहनः
अकायो भक्तकायस्थः कालज्ञानी कलावपुः ॥
1.98.m: sleeping on the earth, maker of prosperity, prosperity, ornament, vehicle of beings, / bodiless, residing in the bodies of his devotees, knower of time, having the arts as his body;

1.98.s:
satyavratamahātyāgī niṣṭhāśāntiparāyaṇaḥ
parārthavṛttir varado viviktaḥ śrutisāgaraḥ //
1.98.d:
सत्यव्रतमहात्यागी निष्ठाशान्तिपरायणः
परार्थवृत्तिर् वरदो विविक्तः श्रुतिसागरः ॥
1.98.m: keeper of vows of truth, great renunciant, dedicated to steadfastness and peace, / acting for the sake of others, giver of boons, solitary, ocean of revelation;

1.98.s:
anirviṇṇo guṇagrāhī kalaṅkāṅkaḥ kalaṅkahā
svabhāvarudro madhyasthaḥ śatrughno madhyanāśakaḥ //
1.98.d:
अनिर्विण्णो गुणग्राही कलङ्काङ्कः कलङ्कहा
स्वभावरुद्रो मध्यस्थः शत्रुघ्नो मध्यनाशकः ॥
1.98.m: undepressed, receptive of virtues, marked with a stain, remover of stains, / Rudra by nature, impartial, slayer of enemies, destroyer of the middle;

1.98.s:
śikhaṇḍī kavacī śūlī caṇḍī muṇḍī ca kuṇḍalī
mekhalī kavacī khaḍgī māyī saṃsārasārathiḥ //
1.98.d:
शिखण्डी कवची शूली चण्डी मुण्डी च कुण्डली
मेखली कवची खड्गी मायी संसारसारथिः ॥
1.98.m: having a topknot, armored, trident-bearer, fierce, shaven-headed, wearing earrings, / wearing a girdle, armored, sword-bearer, wielder of illusion, charioteer of saṃsāra;

1.98.s:
amṛtyuḥ sarvadṛk siṃhas tejorāśir mahāmaṇiḥ
asaṃkhyeyo 'prameyātmā vīryavān kāryakovidaḥ //
1.98.d:
अमृत्युः सर्वदृक् सिंहस् तेजोराशिर् महामणिः
असंख्येयो ऽप्रमेयात्मा वीर्यवान् कार्यकोविदः ॥
1.98.m: deathless, all-seeing, lion, mass of brilliance, great jewel, / innumerable, immeasurable in soul, valorous, skilled in action;

1.98.s:
vedyo vedārthavidgoptā sarvācāro munīśvaraḥ
anuttamo durādharṣo madhuraḥ priyadarśanaḥ //
1.98.d:
वेद्यो वेदार्थविद्गोप्ता सर्वाचारो मुनीश्वरः
अनुत्तमो दुराधर्षो मधुरः प्रियदर्शनः ॥
1.98.m: to be known, knower of Vedic meaning, protector, of all observances, lord of sages, / unsurpassed, unassailable, sweet, pleasing to look at;

1.98.s:
sureśaḥ śaraṇaṃ sarvaḥ śabdabrahma satāṃ gatiḥ
kālabhakṣaḥ kalaṅkāriḥ kaṅkaṇīkṛtavāsukiḥ //
1.98.d:
सुरेशः शरणं सर्वः शब्दब्रह्म सतां गतिः
कालभक्षः कलङ्कारिः कङ्कणीकृतवासुकिः ॥
1.98.m: lord of the gods, refuge, all, Brahman as sound, refuge of the good, / devourer of time, enemy of blemish, who made Vāsuki his bracelet;

1.98.s:
maheṣvāso mahībhartā niṣkalaṅko viśṛṅkhalaḥ
dyumaṇis taraṇir dhanyaḥ siddhidaḥ siddhisādhanaḥ //
1.98.d:
महेष्वासो महीभर्ता निष्कलङ्को विशृङ्खलः
द्युमणिस् तरणिर् धन्यः सिद्धिदः सिद्धिसाधनः ॥
1.98.m: wielder of a great bow, bearer of the earth, stainless, unchained, / jewel of the sky, the sun, blessed, giver of perfection, means of perfection;

1.98.s:
nivṛttaḥ saṃvṛtaḥ śilpo vyūḍhorasko mahābhujaḥ
ekajyotir nirātaṅko naro nārāyaṇapriyaḥ //
1.98.d:
निवृत्तः संवृतः शिल्पो व्यूढोरस्को महाभुजः
एकज्योतिर् निरातङ्को नरो नारायणप्रियः ॥
1.98.m: turned inward, covered, artisan, broad-chested, mighty-armed, / sole light, free from distress, Nara, dear to Nārāyaṇa;

1.98.s:
nirlepo niṣprapañcātmā nirvyagro vyagranāśanaḥ
stavyastavapriyaḥ stotā vyāsamūrtiranākulaḥ //
1.98.d:
निर्लेपो निष्प्रपञ्चात्मा निर्व्यग्रो व्यग्रनाशनः
स्तव्यस्तवप्रियः स्तोता व्यासमूर्तिरनाकुलः ॥
1.98.m: unstained, free from the manifold world, undisturbed, destroyer of agitation, / worthy of praise, fond of praise, praiser, having Vyāsa's form, unperturbed;

1.98.s:
niravadyapadopāyo vidyārāśiravikramaḥ
praśāntabuddhirakṣudraḥ kṣudrahā nityasundaraḥ //
1.98.d:
निरवद्यपदोपायो विद्याराशिरविक्रमः
प्रशान्तबुद्धिरक्षुद्रः क्षुद्रहा नित्यसुन्दरः ॥
1.98.m: path to the flawless state, mass of wisdom, of unhindered stride, / having a tranquil mind, not mean, destroyer of the mean, eternally handsome;

1.98.s:
dhairyāgryadhuryo dhātrīśaḥ śākalyaḥ śarvarīpatiḥ
paramārthagurur dṛṣṭir gurur āśritavatsalaḥ //
1.98.d:
धैर्याग्र्यधुर्यो धात्रीशः शाकल्यः शर्वरीपतिः
परमार्थगुरुर् दृष्टिर् गुरुर् आश्रितवत्सलः ॥
1.98.m: foremost among the steadfast, lord of the earth, Śākalya, lord of the night, / teacher of the highest truth, sight, guru, affectionate to those who take refuge;

1.98.s:
raso rasajñaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvasattvāvalaṃbanaḥ
evaṃ nāmnāṃ sahasreṇa tuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam //
1.98.d:
रसो रसज्ञः सर्वज्ञः सर्वसत्त्वावलंबनः
एवं नाम्नां सहस्रेण तुष्टाव वृषभध्वजम् ॥
1.98.m: essence, knower of essence, omniscient, support of all beings. / In this way, with a thousand names, he praised the bull-bannered lord.

1.98.s:
snāpayāmāsa ca vibhuḥ pūjayāmāsa paṅkajaiḥ
parīkṣārthaṃ hareḥ pūjākamaleṣu maheśvaraḥ //
1.98.d:
स्नापयामास च विभुः पूजयामास पङ्कजैः
परीक्षार्थं हरेः पूजाकमलेषु महेश्वरः ॥
1.98.m: And the all-pervading lord bathed him, and worshipped him with lotuses. / In order to test Hari, Maheśvara, among the worship-lotuses,

1.98.s:
gopayāmāsa kamalaṃ tadaikaṃ bhuvaneśvaraḥ
hṛtapuṣpo haristatra kimidaṃ tvabhyacintayat //
1.98.d:
गोपयामास कमलं तदैकं भुवनेश्वरः
हृतपुष्पो हरिस्तत्र किमिदं त्वभ्यचिन्तयत् ॥
1.98.m: Then the lord of the world concealed one lotus; / finding a flower stolen there, Hari thought, “What is this?”

1.98.s:
jñātvā svanetramuddhṛtya sarvasattvāvalambanam
pūjayāmāsa bhāvena nāmnā tena jagadgurum //
1.98.d:
ज्ञात्वा स्वनेत्रमुद्धृत्य सर्वसत्त्वावलम्बनम्
पूजयामास भावेन नाम्ना तेन जगद्गुरुम् ॥
1.98.m: Having realized [this], he plucked out his own eye, the support of all living beings, / and devotedly worshipped the guru of the universe with that name.

1.98.s:
tatastatra vibhurdṛṣṭvā tathābhūtaṃ haro harim
tasmādavatatārāśu maṇḍalātpāvakasya ca //
1.98.d:
ततस्तत्र विभुर्दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतं हरो हरिम्
तस्मादवतताराशु मण्डलात्पावकस्य च ॥
1.98.m: Then, seeing Hari [acting] thus there, Hara, the all-pervading lord, / quickly descended from that orb of fire:

1.98.s:
koṭibhāskarasaṃkāśaṃ jaṭāmukuṭamaṇḍitam
jvālāmālāvṛtaṃ divyaṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraṃ bhayaṅkaram //
1.98.d:
कोटिभास्करसंकाशं जटामुकुटमण्डितम्
ज्वालामालावृतं दिव्यं तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रं भयङ्करम् ॥
1.98.m: Resembling ten million suns, adorned with a crown of matted locks, / surrounded by a wreath of flames, divine, sharp-fanged, and terrifying,

1.98.s:
śūlaṭaṅkagadācakrakuntapāśadharaṃ haram
varādabhayahastaṃ ca dvīpicarmottarīyakam //
1.98.d:
शूलटङ्कगदाचक्रकुन्तपाशधरं हरम्
वरादभयहस्तं च द्वीपिचर्मोत्तरीयकम् ॥
1.98.m: Bearing a trident, chisel, mace, discus, spear, and noose, / Hara, with hands bestowing boons and freedom from fear, had a leopard skin as an upper garment.

1.98.s:
itthaṃbhūtaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā bhavaṃ bhasmavibhūṣitam
hṛṣṭo namaścakārāśu devadevaṃ janārdanaḥ //
1.98.d:
इत्थंभूतं तदा दृष्ट्वा भवं भस्मविभूषितम्
हृष्टो नमश्चकाराशु देवदेवं जनार्दनः ॥
1.98.m: Seeing Bhava thus adorned with sacred ash, / delighted Janārdana quickly bowed to the god of gods.

1.98.s:
dudruvustaṃ parikramya sendrā devāstrilocanam
cacāla brahmabhuvanaṃ cakampe ca vasuṃdharā //
1.98.d:
दुद्रुवुस्तं परिक्रम्य सेन्द्रा देवास्त्रिलोचनम्
चचाल ब्रह्मभुवनं चकम्पे च वसुंधरा ॥
1.98.m: Circumambulating that three-eyed god, the gods along with Indra fled; / the world of Brahmā shook, and the earth trembled.

1.98.s:
dadāha tejastacchaṃbhoḥ prāntaṃ vai śatayojanam
adhastāccordhvataścaiva hāhetyakṛta bhūtale //
1.98.d:
ददाह तेजस्तच्छंभोः प्रान्तं वै शतयोजनम्
अधस्ताच्चोर्ध्वतश्चैव हाहेत्यकृत भूतले ॥
1.98.m: That splendour of Śambhu burned for a boundary of a hundred yojanas, / both below and above, and on the surface of the earth they cried “Alas! Alas!”

1.98.s:
tadā prāha mahādevaḥ prahasanniva śaṅkaraḥ
samprekṣya praṇayādviṣṇuṃ kṛtāñjalipuṭaṃ sthitam //
1.98.d:
तदा प्राह महादेवः प्रहसन्निव शङ्करः
सम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रणयाद्विष्णुं कृताञ्जलिपुटं स्थितम् ॥
1.98.m: Then Mahādeva Śaṅkara, as if smiling, / looking with affection upon Viṣṇu standing with folded hands, spoke:

1.98.s:
jñātaṃ mayedamadhunā devakāryaṃ janārdana
sudarśanākhyaṃ cakraṃ ca dadāmi tava śobhanam //
1.98.d:
ज्ञातं मयेदमधुना देवकार्यं जनार्दन
सुदर्शनाख्यं चक्रं च ददामि तव शोभनम् ॥
1.98.m: “This task of the gods has now been understood by me, O Janārdana; / I give you the splendid discus named Sudarśana.

1.98.s:
yadrūpaṃ bhavatā dṛṣṭaṃ sarvalokabhayaṃkaram
hitāya tava yatnena tava bhāvāya suvrata //
1.98.d:
यद्रूपं भवता दृष्टं सर्वलोकभयंकरम्
हिताय तव यत्नेन तव भावाय सुव्रत ॥
1.98.m: The terrifying form seen by you that frightens all the worlds / [was assumed] with effort for your welfare, for your devotion, O one of noble vows.

1.98.s:
śāntaṃ raṇājire viṣṇo devānāṃ duḥkhasādhanam
śāntasya cāstraṃ śāntaḥ syāc chāntenāstreṇa kiṃ phalam //
1.98.d:
शान्तं रणाजिरे विष्णो देवानां दुःखसाधनम्
शान्तस्य चास्त्रं शान्तः स्याच् छान्तेनास्त्रेण किं फलम् ॥
1.98.m: A peaceful [disposition] on the battlefield, O Viṣṇu, causes grief to the gods; / a peaceful weapon belongs to one who is peaceful—what is the fruit of a peaceful weapon?

1.98.s:
śāntasya samare cāstraṃ śāntireva tapasvinām
yoddhuḥ śāntyā balacchedaḥ parasya balavṛddhidaḥ //
1.98.d:
शान्तस्य समरे चास्त्रं शान्तिरेव तपस्विनाम्
योद्धुः शान्त्या बलच्छेदः परस्य बलवृद्धिदः ॥
1.98.m: The weapon of one who is peaceful in battle is only the peace of ascetics; / through the peacefulness of a warrior comes the destruction of strength, while giving increase to an enemy's strength.

1.98.s:
devairaśāntairyadrūpaṃ madīyaṃ bhāvayāvyayam
kimāyudhena kāryaṃ vai yoddhuṃ devārisūdana //
1.98.d:
देवैरशान्तैर्यद्रूपं मदीयं भावयाव्ययम्
किमायुधेन कार्यं वै योद्धुं देवारिसूदन ॥
1.98.m: Meditate upon this imperishable form of mine as [conceived] by the unpeaceful gods; / what is to be done with a weapon if one does not fight, O slayer of the enemies of the gods?

1.98.s:
kṣamā yudhi na kāryaṃ vai yoddhuṃ devārisūdana
anāgate vyatīte ca daurbalye svajanotkare //
1.98.d:
क्षमा युधि न कार्यं वै योद्धुं देवारिसूदन
अनागते व्यतीते च दौर्बल्ये स्वजनोत्करे ॥
1.98.m: Forbearance is not to be exercised in battle to fight, O slayer of the enemies of the gods, / [nor] in what is yet to come, nor in what has passed, nor in weakness toward one’s own people,

1.98.s:
akālike tvadharme ca anarthe vārisūdana
evamuktvā dadau cakraṃ sūryāyutasamaprabham //
1.98.d:
अकालिके त्वधर्मे च अनर्थे वारिसूदन
एवमुक्त्वा ददौ चक्रं सूर्यायुतसमप्रभम् ॥
1.98.m: Nor in untimely unrighteousness, nor in adversity, O slayer of enemies!” / Having spoken thus, he gave him the discus equal in splendour to ten thousand suns.

1.98.s:
netraṃ ca netā jagatāṃ prabhurvai padmasannibham
tadāprabhṛti taṃ prāhuḥ padmākṣamiti suvratam //
1.98.d:
नेत्रं च नेता जगतां प्रभुर्वै पद्मसन्निभम्
तदाप्रभृति तं प्राहुः पद्माक्षमिति सुव्रतम् ॥
1.98.m: And the lord, the leader of the worlds, [restored] his eye resembling a lotus; / from then on, they call that god of noble vows “the lotus-eyed one” (Padmākṣa).

1.98.s:
dattvainaṃ nayanaṃ cakraṃ viṣṇave nīlalohitaḥ
pasparśa ca karābhyāṃ vai suśubhābhyāmuvāca ha //
1.98.d:
दत्त्वैनं नयनं चक्रं विष्णवे नीललोहितः
पस्पर्श च कराभ्यां वै सुशुभाभ्यामुवाच ह ॥
1.98.m: Having given this eye and discus to Viṣṇu, Nīlalohita / touched him with both of his exceedingly auspicious hands and spoke:

1.98.s:
varado 'haṃ varaśreṣṭha varānvaraya cepsitān
bhaktyā vaśīkṛto nūnaṃ tvayāhaṃ puruṣottama //
1.98.d:
वरदो ऽहं वरश्रेष्ठ वरान्वरय चेप्सितान्
भक्त्या वशीकृतो नूनं त्वयाहं पुरुषोत्तम ॥
1.98.m: “I am the bestower of boons, O best among the noble; choose your desired boons! / Indeed, O Puruṣottama, I have been won over by you through devotion.”

1.98.s:
ityukto devadevena devadevaṃ praṇamya tam
tvayi bhaktirmahādeva prasīda varamuttamam //
1.98.d:
इत्युक्तो देवदेवेन देवदेवं प्रणम्य तम्
त्वयि भक्तिर्महादेव प्रसीद वरमुत्तमम् ॥
1.98.m: Addressed thus by the god of gods, having bowed to that god of gods, [he said]: / “Let there be devotion to you, O Mahādeva; be gracious with this supreme boon!

1.98.s:
nānyamicchāmi bhaktānām ārtayo nāsti yatprabho
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya dayāvān sutarāṃ bhavaḥ //
1.98.d:
नान्यमिच्छामि भक्तानाम् आर्तयो नास्ति यत्प्रभो
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य दयावान् सुतरां भवः ॥
1.98.m: I desire no other, for which there is no distress for devotees, O Lord.” / Hearing those words of his, Bhava, being exceedingly compassionate,

1.98.s:
pasparśa ca dadau tasmai śraddhāṃ śītāṃśubhūṣaṇaḥ
prāha caivaṃ mahādevaḥ paramātmānamacyutam //
1.98.d:
पस्पर्श च ददौ तस्मै श्रद्धां शीतांशुभूषणः
प्राह चैवं महादेवः परमात्मानमच्युतम् ॥
1.98.m: Touched him, and the god adorned with the cool-rayed moon granted him faith; / and Mahādeva spoke thus to the infallible Supreme Self:

1.98.s:
mayi bhaktaś ca vandyaś ca pūjyaścaiva surāsuraiḥ
bhaviṣyasi na saṃdeho matprasādātsurottama //
1.98.d:
मयि भक्तश् च वन्द्यश् च पूज्यश्चैव सुरासुरैः
भविष्यसि न संदेहो मत्प्रसादात्सुरोत्तम ॥
1.98.m: “Devoted to me, you shall be praised and worshipped by gods and asuras; / there is no doubt, O best of the gods, by my grace.

1.98.s:
yadā satī dakṣaputrī vinindyaiva sulocanā
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ dakṣaṃ bhaviṣyati sureśvarī //
1.98.d:
यदा सती दक्षपुत्री विनिन्द्यैव सुलोचना
मातरं पितरं दक्षं भविष्यति सुरेश्वरी ॥
1.98.m: When Satī, Dakṣa's daughter, the fair-eyed queen of the gods, / having reviled her mother and father Dakṣa, will become

1.98.s:
divyā haimavatī viṣṇo tadā tvamapi suvrata
bhaginīṃ tava kalyāṇīṃ devīṃ haimavatīmumām //
1.98.d:
दिव्या हैमवती विष्णो तदा त्वमपि सुव्रत
भगिनीं तव कल्याणीं देवीं हैमवतीमुमाम् ॥
1.98.m: The divine daughter of Himavat, O Viṣṇu, then you too, O one of noble vows, / [shall have] as your auspicious sister that goddess Umā, daughter of Himavat.

1.98.s:
niyogād brahmaṇaḥ sādhvīṃ pradāsyasi mamaiva tām
matsaṃbandhī ca lokānāṃ madhye pūjyo bhaviṣyasi //
1.98.d:
नियोगाद् ब्रह्मणः साध्वीं प्रदास्यसि ममैव ताम्
मत्संबन्धी च लोकानां मध्ये पूज्यो भविष्यसि ॥
1.98.m: By Brahmā’s instruction, you shall give that virtuous lady to me alone; / and as my kinsman, you shall be worshipped among the worlds.

1.98.s:
māṃ divyena ca bhāvena tadāprabhṛti śaṅkaram
drakṣyase ca prasannena mitrabhūtamivātmanā //
1.98.d:
मां दिव्येन च भावेन तदाप्रभृति शङ्करम्
द्रक्ष्यसे च प्रसन्नेन मित्रभूतमिवात्मना ॥
1.98.m: From then on, with a divine disposition, you shall see me, Śaṅkara, / with a pleased mind, as though a friend to yourself.”

1.98.s:
ityuktvāntardadhe rudro bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ
janārdano 'pi bhagavān devānāmapi saṃnidhau //
1.98.d:
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे रुद्रो भगवान्नीललोहितः
जनार्दनो ऽपि भगवान् देवानामपि संनिधौ ॥
1.98.m: Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord Rudra Nīlalohita vanished; / and the blessed Janārdana too, in the presence of the gods,

1.98.s:
ayācata mahādevaṃ brahmāṇaṃ munibhiḥ samam
mayā proktaṃ stavaṃ divyaṃ padmayone suśobhanam //
1.98.d:
अयाचत महादेवं ब्रह्माणं मुनिभिः समम्
मया प्रोक्तं स्तवं दिव्यं पद्मयोने सुशोभनम् ॥
1.98.m: Prayed to Mahādeva and to Brahmā along with the sages: / “The divine and most splendid praise spoken by me, O lotus-born one,

1.98.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi śrāvayedvā dvijottamān
pratināmni hiraṇyasya tat tasya phalam āpnuyāt //
1.98.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि श्रावयेद्वा द्विजोत्तमान्
प्रतिनाम्नि हिरण्यस्य तत् तस्य फलम् आप्नुयात् ॥
1.98.m: Whoever reads it, listens to it, or recites it to the best of the twice-born, / shall obtain the fruit of [a gift of] gold for every name.

1.98.s:
aśvamedhasahasreṇa phalaṃ bhavati tasya vai
ghṛtādyaiḥ snāpayedrudraṃ sthālyā vai kalaśaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.98.d:
अश्वमेधसहस्रेण फलं भवति तस्य वै
घृताद्यैः स्नापयेद्रुद्रं स्थाल्या वै कलशैः शुभैः ॥
1.98.m: He indeed obtains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices. / He who bathes Rudra with ghee and the like from a dish or auspicious vessels,

1.98.s:
nāmnāṃ sahasreṇānena śraddhayā śivamīśvaram
so 'pi yajñasahasrasya phalaṃ labdhvāsureśvaraiḥ //
1.98.d:
नाम्नां सहस्रेणानेन श्रद्धया शिवमीश्वरम्
सो ऽपि यज्ञसहस्रस्य फलं लब्ध्वासुरेश्वरैः ॥
1.98.m: With faith in Śiva the Lord, with this thousand names, / having obtained the fruit of a thousand sacrifices, he too becomes worshipped

1.98.s:
pūjyo bhavati rudrasya prītirbhavati tasya vai
tathāstviti tathā prāha padmayonerjanārdanam //
1.98.d:
पूज्यो भवति रुद्रस्य प्रीतिर्भवति तस्य वै
तथास्त्विति तथा प्राह पद्मयोनेर्जनार्दनम् ॥
1.98.m: By the chiefs of the asuras, and the affection of Rudra is his.” / “So be it!” said the lotus-born one to Janārdana.

1.98.s:
jagmatuḥ praṇipatyainaṃ devadevaṃ jagadgurum
tasmānnāmnāṃ sahasreṇa pūjayed anagho dvijāḥ //
1.98.d:
जग्मतुः प्रणिपत्यैनं देवदेवं जगद्गुरुम्
तस्मान्नाम्नां सहस्रेण पूजयेद् अनघो द्विजाः ॥
1.98.m: Having bowed to that god of gods, the guru of the universe, both departed. / Therefore, O sinless twice-born ones, one should worship with the thousand names;

1.98.s: japennāmnāṃ sahasraṃ ca sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
1.98.d: जपेन्नाम्नां सहस्रं च स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
1.98.m: And one who recites the thousand names attains the supreme goal.

1.99.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
saṃbhavaḥ sūcito devyās tvayā sūta mahāmate
savistaraṃ vadasvādya satītve ca yathātatham //
1.99.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
संभवः सूचितो देव्यास् त्वया सूत महामते
सविस्तरं वदस्वाद्य सतीत्वे च यथातथम् ॥
1.99.m: The sages said: / “The manifestation of the goddess has been indicated by you, O wise Sūta; / tell it now in full detail and accurately regarding her state as Satī,

1.99.s:
menājatvaṃ mahādevyā dakṣayajñavimardanam
viṣṇunā ca kathaṃ dattā devadevāya śaṃbhave //
1.99.d:
मेनाजत्वं महादेव्या दक्षयज्ञविमर्दनम्
विष्णुना च कथं दत्ता देवदेवाय शंभवे ॥
1.99.m: How Mahādevī was born of Menā, the crushing of Dakṣa's sacrifice, / and how she was given by Viṣṇu to Śambhu, the god of gods,

1.99.s:
kalyāṇaṃ vā kathaṃ tasya vaktumarhasi sāṃpratam
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sūtaḥ paurāṇikottamaḥ //
1.99.d:
कल्याणं वा कथं तस्य वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम्
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सूतः पौराणिकोत्तमः ॥
1.99.m: Or how her marriage [took place]—you ought to tell it now.” / Having heard those words of theirs, Sūta, the best of the Purāṇa reciters,

1.99.s:
saṃbhavaṃ ca mahādevyāḥ prāha teṣāṃ mahātmanām
brahmaṇā kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ daṇḍine tat suvistaram //
1.99.d:
संभवं च महादेव्याः प्राह तेषां महात्मनाम्
ब्रह्मणा कथितं पूर्वं दण्डिने तत् सुविस्तरम् ॥
1.99.m: Spoke of the manifestation of the Great Goddess to those great-souled ones, / as it was told in full detail long ago by Brahmā to Daṇḍin,

1.99.s:
yuṣmābhir vai kumārāya tena vyāsāya dhīmate
tasmādahamupaśrutya pravadāmi suvistaram //
1.99.d:
युष्माभिर् वै कुमाराय तेन व्यासाय धीमते
तस्मादहमुपश्रुत्य प्रवदामि सुविस्तरम् ॥
1.99.m: By you to Kumāra, and by him to the wise Vyāsa; / having heard it from him, I tell it in full detail.

1.99.s:
vacanādvo mahābhāgāḥ praṇamyomāṃ tathā bhavam
sā bhagākhyā jagaddhātrī liṅgamūrtestrivedikā //
1.99.d:
वचनाद्वो महाभागाः प्रणम्योमां तथा भवम्
सा भगाख्या जगद्धात्री लिङ्गमूर्तेस्त्रिवेदिका ॥
1.99.m: At your word, O fortunate ones, having bowed to Umā and likewise to Bhava: / She who is called Bhaga is the supporter of the universe, the threefold altar of the liṅga-form.

1.99.s:
liṅgastu bhagavāndvābhyāṃ jagatsṛṣṭirdvijottamāḥ
liṅgamūrtiḥ śivo jyotis tamasaścopari sthitaḥ //
1.99.d:
लिङ्गस्तु भगवान्द्वाभ्यां जगत्सृष्टिर्द्विजोत्तमाः
लिङ्गमूर्तिः शिवो ज्योतिस् तमसश्चोपरि स्थितः ॥
1.99.m: The liṅga is the Lord; from both of them comes the creation of the world, O best of the twice-born. / Śiva in the form of the liṅga is light, situated above the darkness.

1.99.s:
liṅgavedisamāyogād ardhanārīśvarobhavat
brahmāṇaṃ vidadhe devam agre putraṃ caturmukham //
1.99.d:
लिङ्गवेदिसमायोगाद् अर्धनारीश्वरोभवत्
ब्रह्माणं विदधे देवम् अग्रे पुत्रं चतुर्मुखम् ॥
1.99.m: Through union with the altar of the liṅga, he became Ardhanārīśvara; / first he brought forth the god Brahmā, his four-faced son.

1.99.s:
prāhiṇoti sma tasyaiva jñānaṃ jñānamayo haraḥ
viśvādhiko 'sau bhagavān ardhanārīśvaro vibhuḥ //
1.99.d:
प्राहिणोति स्म तस्यैव ज्ञानं ज्ञानमयो हरः
विश्वाधिको ऽसौ भगवान् अर्धनारीश्वरो विभुः ॥
1.99.m: Hara, consisting of knowledge, transmitted knowledge to him alone; / that Lord Ardhanārīśvara is all-pervading and transcends the universe.

1.99.s:
hiraṇyagarbhaṃ taṃ devo jāyamānamapaśyata
so 'pi rudraṃ mahādevaṃ brahmāpaśyata śaṅkaram //
1.99.d:
हिरण्यगर्भं तं देवो जायमानमपश्यत
सो ऽपि रुद्रं महादेवं ब्रह्मापश्यत शङ्करम् ॥
1.99.m: The god saw that Hiraṇyagarbha being born; / and Brahmā also saw Rudra, Mahādeva Śaṅkara.

1.99.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃsthitaṃ devam ardhanārīśvaraṃ prabhum
tuṣṭāva vāgbhir iṣṭābhir varadaṃ vārijodbhavaḥ //
1.99.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा संस्थितं देवम् अर्धनारीश्वरं प्रभुम्
तुष्टाव वाग्भिर् इष्टाभिर् वरदं वारिजोद्भवः ॥
1.99.m: Seeing that lord Ardhanārīśvara standing there, / the lotus-born one praised the bestower of boons with desired hymns of praise:

1.99.s:
vibhajasveti viśveśaṃ viśvātmānamajo vibhuḥ
sasarja devīṃ vāmāṅgāt patnīṃ caivātmanaḥ samām //
1.99.d:
विभजस्वेति विश्वेशं विश्वात्मानमजो विभुः
ससर्ज देवीं वामाङ्गात् पत्नीं चैवात्मनः समाम् ॥
1.99.m: “Divide yourself!” the unborn lord [said] to the lord of all, the Self of all; / from his left side he brought forth the goddess, his wife equal to himself.

1.99.s:
śraddhā hyasya śubhā patnī tataḥ puṃsaḥ purātanī
saivājñayā vibhordevī dakṣaputrī babhūva ha //
1.99.d:
श्रद्धा ह्यस्य शुभा पत्नी ततः पुंसः पुरातनी
सैवाज्ञया विभोर्देवी दक्षपुत्री बभूव ह ॥
1.99.m: Faith (Śraddhā) indeed was the ancient auspicious wife of that Puruṣa; / then, by the Lord's command, that goddess became the daughter of Dakṣa.

1.99.s:
satīsaṃjñā tadā sā vai rudramevāśritā patim
dakṣaṃ vinindya kālena devī mainā hyabhūtpunaḥ //
1.99.d:
सतीसंज्ञा तदा सा वै रुद्रमेवाश्रिता पतिम्
दक्षं विनिन्द्य कालेन देवी मैना ह्यभूत्पुनः ॥
1.99.m: Bearing the name Satī at that time, she took refuge in Rudra alone as her husband. / In time, having censured Dakṣa, the goddess became [the daughter] of Menā.

1.99.s:
nāradasyaiva dakṣo 'pi śāpādevaṃ vinindya ca
avajñādurmado dakṣo devadevamumāpatim //
1.99.d:
नारदस्यैव दक्षो ऽपि शापादेवं विनिन्द्य च
अवज्ञादुर्मदो दक्षो देवदेवमुमापतिम् ॥
1.99.m: And Dakṣa also, because of Nārada's curse, having reviled in this way, / Dakṣa, mad with contempt [towards] the God of gods, the lord of Umā,

1.99.s:
anādṛtya kṛtiṃ jñātvā satī dakṣeṇa tatkṣaṇāt
bhasmīkṛtvātmano dehaṃ yogamārgeṇa sā punaḥ //
1.99.d:
अनादृत्य कृतिं ज्ञात्वा सती दक्षेण तत्क्षणात्
भस्मीकृत्वात्मनो देहं योगमार्गेण सा पुनः ॥
1.99.m: having shown disregard and Satī having known that deed done by Dakṣa, instantly / having reduced her own body to ashes through the path of yoga, she again

1.99.s:
babhūva pārvatī devī tapasā ca gireḥ prabhoḥ
jñātvaitadbhagavān bhargo dadāha ruṣitaḥ prabhuḥ //
1.99.d:
बभूव पार्वती देवी तपसा च गिरेः प्रभोः
ज्ञात्वैतद्भगवान् भर्गो ददाह रुषितः प्रभुः ॥
1.99.m: became the goddess Pārvatī through the tapas of the mountain, the lord. / Knowing this, the furious Lord Bharga burned [Dakṣa's sacrifice].

1.99.s:
dakṣasya vipulaṃ yajñaṃ cyāvaner vacanādapi
cyavanasya suto dhīmān dadhīca iti viśrutaḥ //
1.99.d:
दक्षस्य विपुलं यज्ञं च्यावनेर् वचनादपि
च्यवनस्य सुतो धीमान् दधीच इति विश्रुतः ॥
1.99.m: The vast sacrifice of Dakṣa [was destroyed], and also according to the word of the son of Cyavana— / the wise son of Cyavana, renowned as Dadhīca.

1.99.s:
vijitya viṣṇuṃ samare prasādāt tryaṃbakasya ca
viṣṇunā lokapālāṃś ca śaśāpa ca munīśvaraḥ //
1.99.d:
विजित्य विष्णुं समरे प्रसादात् त्र्यंबकस्य च
विष्णुना लोकपालांश् च शशाप च मुनीश्वरः ॥
1.99.m: Having conquered Viṣṇu in battle by the grace of Tryambaka, / the lord of sages cursed the guardians of the worlds together with Viṣṇu:

1.99.s:
rudrasya krodhajenaiva vahninā haviṣā surāḥ
vināśo vai kṣaṇādeva māyayā śaṅkarasya vai //
1.99.d:
रुद्रस्य क्रोधजेनैव वह्निना हविषा सुराः
विनाशो वै क्षणादेव मायया शङ्करस्य वै ॥
1.99.m: "O gods, by the very fire born of Rudra's wrath, with [your own] oblation, / there shall indeed be destruction in a mere moment through the māyā of Śaṅkara!"

1.100.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
vijitya viṣṇunā sārdhaṃ bhagavānparameśvaraḥ
sarvāndadhīcavacanāt kathaṃ bheje maheśvaraḥ //
1.100.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
विजित्य विष्णुना सार्धं भगवान्परमेश्वरः
सर्वान्दधीचवचनात् कथं भेजे महेश्वरः ॥
1.100.m: The sages said: / "Having conquered along with Viṣṇu, how did the Lord, the supreme master, / Maheśvara, resort to everyone according to the words of Dadhīca?"

1.100.s:
sūta uvāca
dakṣayajñe suvipule devān viṣṇupurogamān
dadāha bhagavān rudraḥ sarvān munigaṇān api //
1.100.d:
सूत उवाच
दक्षयज्ञे सुविपुले देवान् विष्णुपुरोगमान्
ददाह भगवान् रुद्रः सर्वान् मुनिगणान् अपि ॥
1.100.m: Sūta said: / "In the vast sacrifice of Dakṣa, the Lord Rudra burned / the gods headed by Viṣṇu and all the hosts of sages.

1.100.s:
bhadro nāma gaṇastena preṣitaḥ parameṣṭhinā
viprayogena devyā vai duḥsahenaiva suvratāḥ //
1.100.d:
भद्रो नाम गणस्तेन प्रेषितः परमेष्ठिना
विप्रयोगेन देव्या वै दुःसहेनैव सुव्रताः ॥
1.100.m: A gaṇa named Bhadra was sent by that Supreme Lord / because of the unbearable separation from the goddess, O you of noble vows!

1.100.s:
so 'sṛjad vīrabhadraś ca gaṇeśānromajāñchubhān
gaṇeśvaraiḥ samāruhya rathaṃ bhadraḥ pratāpavān //
1.100.d:
सो ऽसृजद् वीरभद्रश् च गणेशान्रोमजाञ्छुभान्
गणेश्वरैः समारुह्य रथं भद्रः प्रतापवान् ॥
1.100.m: And he, Vīrabhadra, created auspicious leaders of the gaṇas born of his hair. / Ascending a chariot with the leaders of the gaṇas, the glorious Bhadra

1.100.s:
gantuṃ cakre matiṃ yasya sārathirbhagavānajaḥ
gaṇeśvarāś ca te sarve vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ //
1.100.d:
गन्तुं चक्रे मतिं यस्य सारथिर्भगवानजः
गणेश्वराश् च ते सर्वे विविधायुधपाणयः ॥
1.100.m: set his mind on marching—he whose charioteer was the unborn Lord [Brahmā]! / And all those leaders of the gaṇas, with various weapons in hand,

1.100.s:
vimānairviśvato bhadrais tamanvayuratho surāḥ
himavacchikhare ramye hemaśṛṅge suśobhane //
1.100.d:
विमानैर्विश्वतो भद्रैस् तमन्वयुरथो सुराः
हिमवच्छिखरे रम्ये हेमशृङ्गे सुशोभने ॥
1.100.m: followed him in aerial chariots on all sides, O auspicious gods. / On the delightful peak of Himavat, adorned with golden crests,

1.100.s:
yajñavāṭas tathā tasya gaṅgādvārasamīpataḥ
taddeśe caiva vikhyātaṃ śubhaṃ kanakhalaṃ dvijāḥ //
1.100.d:
यज्ञवाटस् तथा तस्य गङ्गाद्वारसमीपतः
तद्देशे चैव विख्यातं शुभं कनखलं द्विजाः ॥
1.100.m: was his sacrificial enclosure, near the gate of the Gaṅgā (Gaṅgādvāra), / in that renowned and auspicious region of Kanakhala, O twice-born!

1.100.s:
dagdhuṃ vai preṣitaścāsau bhagavān parameṣṭhinā
tadotpāto babhūvātha lokānāṃ bhayaśaṃsanaḥ //
1.100.d:
दग्धुं वै प्रेषितश्चासौ भगवान् परमेष्ठिना
तदोत्पातो बभूवाथ लोकानां भयशंसनः ॥
1.100.m: Sent indeed by the Supreme Lord to burn [it], / then an omen arose, proclaiming fear unto the worlds.

1.100.s:
parvatāś ca vyaśīryanta pracakampe vasuṃdharā
marutaś cāpy aghūrṇanta cukṣubhe makarālayaḥ //
1.100.d:
पर्वताश् च व्यशीर्यन्त प्रचकम्पे वसुंधरा
मरुतश् चाप्य् अघूर्णन्त चुक्षुभे मकरालयः ॥
1.100.m: Mountains shattered, the earth trembled violently, / the winds whirled about, and the ocean (abode of sea monsters) was agitated.

1.100.s:
agnayo naiva dīpyanti na ca dīpyati bhāskaraḥ
grahāś ca na prakāśyante na devā na ca dānavāḥ //
1.100.d:
अग्नयो नैव दीप्यन्ति न च दीप्यति भास्करः
ग्रहाश् च न प्रकाश्यन्ते न देवा न च दानवाः ॥
1.100.m: Fires did not blaze at all, nor did the sun shine; / planets did not radiate light, nor did the gods, nor the dānavas.

1.100.s:
tataḥ kṣaṇāt praviśyaiva yajñavāṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ
romajaiḥ sahito bhadraḥ kālāgnirivacāparaḥ //
1.100.d:
ततः क्षणात् प्रविश्यैव यज्ञवाटं महात्मनः
रोमजैः सहितो भद्रः कालाग्निरिवचापरः ॥
1.100.m: Then, instantly entering the sacrificial enclosure of the great-souled one / together with those born of his hair, Bhadra was like another fire of cosmic destruction.

1.100.s:
uvāca bhadro bhagavān dakṣaṃ cāmitatejasam
saṃparkādeva dakṣādya munīndevān pinākinā //
1.100.d:
उवाच भद्रो भगवान् दक्षं चामिततेजसम्
संपर्कादेव दक्षाद्य मुनीन्देवान् पिनाकिना ॥
1.100.m: The lordly Bhadra said to Dakṣa of immeasurable splendour: / "Because of your association [with this offense], today, O Dakṣa, by the Pināka-bearer [have I been sent] / to burn the sages, the gods,

1.100.s:
dagdhuṃ saṃpreṣitaś cāhaṃ bhavantaṃ samunīśvaraiḥ
ityuktvā yajñaśālāṃ tāṃ dadāha gaṇapuṅgavaḥ //
1.100.d:
दग्धुं संप्रेषितश् चाहं भवन्तं समुनीश्वरैः
इत्युक्त्वा यज्ञशालां तां ददाह गणपुङ्गवः ॥
1.100.m: and you together with the lords of sages!" / Having spoken thus, the foremost of the gaṇas burned that sacrificial hall.

1.100.s:
gaṇeśvarāś ca saṃkruddhā yūpānutpāṭya cikṣipuḥ
prastotrā saha hotrā ca dagdhaṃ caiva gaṇeśvaraiḥ //
1.100.d:
गणेश्वराश् च संक्रुद्धा यूपानुत्पाट्य चिक्षिपुः
प्रस्तोत्रा सह होत्रा च दग्धं चैव गणेश्वरैः ॥
1.100.m: And the enraged leaders of the gaṇas, having uprooted the sacrificial posts, cast them down. / It was burned by the gaṇa-lords along with the prastotṛ and the hotṛ.

1.100.s:
gṛhītvā gaṇapāḥ sarvān gaṅgāsrotasi cikṣipuḥ
vīrabhadro mahātejāḥ śakrasyodyacchataḥ karam //
1.100.d:
गृहीत्वा गणपाः सर्वान् गङ्गास्रोतसि चिक्षिपुः
वीरभद्रो महातेजाः शक्रस्योद्यच्छतः करम् ॥
1.100.m: Seizing all of them, the protectors of the gaṇas threw them into the current of the Gaṅgā. / Vīrabhadra of great splendour, as Śakra raised his hand,

1.100.s:
vyaṣṭambhayad adīnātmā tathānyeṣāṃ divaukasām
bhagasya netre cotpāṭya karajāgreṇa līlayā //
1.100.d:
व्यष्टम्भयद् अदीनात्मा तथान्येषां दिवौकसाम्
भगस्य नेत्रे चोत्पाट्य करजाग्रेण लीलया ॥
1.100.m: paralysed it, being resolute of soul, and likewise [the limbs] of other celestials. / Plucking out the eyes of Bhaga with the tips of his fingernails in divine play,

1.100.s:
nihatya muṣṭinā dantān pūṣṇaścaivaṃ nyapātayat
tathā candramasaṃ devaṃ pādāṅguṣṭhena līlayā //
1.100.d:
निहत्य मुष्टिना दन्तान् पूष्णश्चैवं न्यपातयत्
तथा चन्द्रमसं देवं पादाङ्गुष्ठेन लीलया ॥
1.100.m: striking Pūṣan with his fist, he knocked out his teeth. / Likewise, with the big toe of his foot, in divine play,

1.100.s:
gharṣayāmāsa bhagavān vīrabhadraḥ pratāpavān
cicheda ca śirastasya śakrasya bhagavānprabhoḥ //
1.100.d:
घर्षयामास भगवान् वीरभद्रः प्रतापवान्
चिछेद च शिरस्तस्य शक्रस्य भगवान्प्रभोः ॥
1.100.m: the glorious Lord Vīrabhadra crushed the moon god, / and the lord severed the head of that Śakra, the master.

1.100.s:
vahnerhastadvayaṃ chittvā jihvāmutpāṭya līlayā
jaghāna mūrdhni pādena vīrabhadro mahābalaḥ //
1.100.d:
वह्नेर्हस्तद्वयं छित्त्वा जिह्वामुत्पाट्य लीलया
जघान मूर्ध्नि पादेन वीरभद्रो महाबलः ॥
1.100.m: Cutting off the two hands of Agni and playfully tearing out his tongue, / Vīrabhadra of great strength struck him on the head with his foot.

1.100.s:
yamasya daṇḍaṃ bhagavān pracicheda svayaṃ prabhuḥ
jaghāna devamīśānaṃ triśūlena mahābalam //
1.100.d:
यमस्य दण्डं भगवान् प्रचिछेद स्वयं प्रभुः
जघान देवमीशानं त्रिशूलेन महाबलम् ॥
1.100.m: The Lord himself cut through the staff of Yama; / he struck the mighty god Īśāna with his trident.

1.100.s:
trayastriṃśatsurānevaṃ vinihatyāprayatnataḥ
trayaś ca triśataṃ teṣāṃ trisāhasraṃ ca līlayā //
1.100.d:
त्रयस्त्रिंशत्सुरानेवं विनिहत्याप्रयत्नतः
त्रयश् च त्रिशतं तेषां त्रिसाहस्रं च लीलया ॥
1.100.m: Having thus effortlessly slain the thirty-three gods, / three hundred of them, and three thousand in divine play,

1.100.s:
trayaṃ caiva surendrāṇāṃ jaghāna ca munīśvarān
anyāṃś ca devān devo 'sau sarvānyuddhāya saṃsthitān //
1.100.d:
त्रयं चैव सुरेन्द्राणां जघान च मुनीश्वरान्
अन्यांश् च देवान् देवो ऽसौ सर्वान्युद्धाय संस्थितान् ॥
1.100.m: and the triad of the rulers of the gods, he struck the lords of sages / and other gods—all those who stood ready for battle,

1.100.s:
jaghāna bhagavān rudraḥ khaḍgamuṣṭyādisāyakaiḥ
atha viṣṇurmahātejāś cakram udyamya mūrchitaḥ //
1.100.d:
जघान भगवान् रुद्रः खड्गमुष्ट्यादिसायकैः
अथ विष्णुर्महातेजाश् चक्रम् उद्यम्य मूर्छितः ॥
1.100.m: the Lord Rudra struck down with sword, fists, arrows, and other [weapons]. / Then Viṣṇu of great splendour, lifting his discus, stupefied,

1.100.s:
yuyodha bhagavāṃstena rudreṇa saha mādhavaḥ
tayoḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ sughoraṃ romaharṣaṇam //
1.100.d:
युयोध भगवांस्तेन रुद्रेण सह माधवः
तयोः समभवद्युद्धं सुघोरं रोमहर्षणम् ॥
1.100.m: the Lord Mādhava fought with that Rudra. / Between the two of them there occurred a most dreadful, hair-raising battle.

1.100.s: viṣṇoryogabalāttasya divyadehāḥ sudāruṇāḥ //
1.100.d: विष्णोर्योगबलात्तस्य दिव्यदेहाः सुदारुणाः ॥
1.100.m: By the power of Viṣṇu's yoga, celestial bodies of terrible ferocity,

1.100.s:
śaṅkhacakragadāhastā asaṃkhyātāś ca jajñire
tānsarvānapi devo 'sau nārāyaṇasamaprabhān //
1.100.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्ता असंख्याताश् च जज्ञिरे
तान्सर्वानपि देवो ऽसौ नारायणसमप्रभान् ॥
1.100.m: holding conch, discus, and mace in hand, were born in innumerable numbers. / Striking all of them, who equalled Nārāyaṇa in radiance,

1.100.s:
nihatya gadayā viṣṇuṃ tāḍayāmāsa mūrdhani
tataścorasi taṃ devaṃ līlayaiva raṇājire //
1.100.d:
निहत्य गदया विष्णुं ताडयामास मूर्धनि
ततश्चोरसि तं देवं लीलयैव रणाजिरे ॥
1.100.m: that god struck Viṣṇu on the head with his mace, / and then struck that god on the chest with mere ease on the battlefield.

1.100.s:
papāta ca tadā bhūmau visaṃjñaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
punarutthāya taṃ hantuṃ cakramudyamya sa prabhuḥ //
1.100.d:
पपात च तदा भूमौ विसंज्ञः पुरुषोत्तमः
पुनरुत्थाय तं हन्तुं चक्रमुद्यम्य स प्रभुः ॥
1.100.m: And then the Supreme Person fell to the ground unconscious. / Rising up again to slay him, raising his discus, the lord,

1.100.s:
krodharaktekṣaṇaḥ śrīmān atiṣṭhat puruṣarṣabhaḥ
tasya cakraṃ ca yadraudraṃ kālādityasamaprabham //
1.100.d:
क्रोधरक्तेक्षणः श्रीमान् अतिष्ठत् पुरुषर्षभः
तस्य चक्रं च यद्रौद्रं कालादित्यसमप्रभम् ॥
1.100.m: the glorious bull among men, stood with eyes red with anger. / And his dreadful discus, equal in splendour to the sun of cosmic destruction,

1.100.s:
vyaṣṭambhayad adīnātmā karasthaṃ na cacāla saḥ
atiṣṭhat stambhitastena śṛṅgavāniva niścalaḥ //
1.100.d:
व्यष्टम्भयद् अदीनात्मा करस्थं न चचाल सः
अतिष्ठत् स्तम्भितस्तेन शृङ्गवानिव निश्चलः ॥
1.100.m: he, resolute of soul, paralysed while still in his hand, so that it did not move. / [Viṣṇu] stood paralysed by him, motionless like a horned mountain.

1.100.s:
tribhiś ca dharṣitaṃ śārṅgaṃ tridhābhūtaṃ prabhostadā
śārṅgakoṭiprasaṅgād vai cicheda ca śiraḥ prabhoḥ //
1.100.d:
त्रिभिश् च धर्षितं शार्ङ्गं त्रिधाभूतं प्रभोस्तदा
शार्ङ्गकोटिप्रसङ्गाद् वै चिछेद च शिरः प्रभोः ॥
1.100.m: Assailed by three [arrows], the lord's Śārṅga bow then split into three pieces; / indeed, by the impact of the tip of the Śārṅga bow, he severed the lord's head.

1.100.s:
chinnaṃ ca nipapātāsu śirastasya rasātale
vāyunā preritaṃ caiva prāṇajena pinākinā //
1.100.d:
छिन्नं च निपपातासु शिरस्तस्य रसातले
वायुना प्रेरितं चैव प्राणजेन पिनाकिना ॥
1.100.m: And his severed head quickly fell into Rasātala; / propelled by the wind born of the life-breath of the Pināka-wielder,

1.100.s:
praviveśa tadā caiva tadīyāhavanīyakam
tat pratidhvastakalaśaṃ bhagnayūpaṃ satoraṇam //
1.100.d:
प्रविवेश तदा चैव तदीयाहवनीयकम्
तत् प्रतिध्वस्तकलशं भग्नयूपं सतोरणम् ॥
1.100.m: it then entered his sacrificial Āhavanīya fire. / Seeing its pitchers smashed, its sacrificial posts broken, with archways down,

1.100.s:
pradīpitamahāśālaṃ dṛṣṭvā yajño 'pi dudruve
taṃ tadā mṛgarūpeṇa dhāvantaṃ gaganaṃ prati //
1.100.d:
प्रदीपितमहाशालं दृष्ट्वा यज्ञो ऽपि दुद्रुवे
तं तदा मृगरूपेण धावन्तं गगनं प्रति ॥
1.100.m: and its great hall set ablaze, the Sacrifice itself fled. / As it was running towards the sky in the form of a deer,

1.100.s:
vīrabhadraḥ samādhāya viśiraskamathākarot
tataḥ prajāpatiṃ dharmaṃ kaśyapaṃ ca jagadgurum //
1.100.d:
वीरभद्रः समाधाय विशिरस्कमथाकरोत्
ततः प्रजापतिं धर्मं कश्यपं च जगद्गुरुम् ॥
1.100.m: Vīrabhadra aimed and then rendered it headless. / Then Dharma the Prajāpati, Kaśyapa the teacher of the world,

1.100.s:
ariṣṭaneminaṃ vīro bahuputraṃ munīśvaram
munim aṅgirasaṃ caiva kṛṣṇāśvaṃ ca mahābalaḥ //
1.100.d:
अरिष्टनेमिनं वीरो बहुपुत्रं मुनीश्वरम्
मुनिम् अङ्गिरसं चैव कृष्णाश्वं च महाबलः ॥
1.100.m: the hero Ariṣṭanemi, the lord of sages Bahuputra, / the sage Aṅgiras, and Kṛṣṇāśva of great strength—

1.100.s:
jaghāna mūrdhni pādena dakṣaṃ caiva yaśasvinam
cicheda ca śirastasya dadāhāgnau dvijottamāḥ //
1.100.d:
जघान मूर्ध्नि पादेन दक्षं चैव यशस्विनम्
चिछेद च शिरस्तस्य ददाहाग्नौ द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.100.m: [all these] and the renowned Dakṣa he struck on the head with his foot, / severed his head, and burned it in the fire, O best of twice-born!

1.100.s:
sarasvatyāś ca nāsāgraṃ devamātustathaiva ca
nikṛtya karajāgreṇa vīrabhadraḥ pratāpavān //
1.100.d:
सरस्वत्याश् च नासाग्रं देवमातुस्तथैव च
निकृत्य करजाग्रेण वीरभद्रः प्रतापवान् ॥
1.100.m: And shearing off the tip of Sarasvatī's nose, and likewise that of the mother of the gods, / with the tip of his fingernail, the glorious Vīrabhadra

1.100.s:
tasthau śriyā vṛto madhye pretasthāne yathā bhavaḥ
etasminneva kāle tu bhagavānpadmasaṃbhavaḥ //
1.100.d:
तस्थौ श्रिया वृतो मध्ये प्रेतस्थाने यथा भवः
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भगवान्पद्मसंभवः ॥
1.100.m: stood enveloped in glory in the midst, like Bhava in a cremation ground. / At that very time, however, the Lord born from the lotus (Brahmā),

1.100.s:
bhadramāha mahātejāḥ prārthayanpraṇataḥ prabhuḥ
alaṃ krodhena vai bhadra naṣṭāścaiva divaukasaḥ //
1.100.d:
भद्रमाह महातेजाः प्रार्थयन्प्रणतः प्रभुः
अलं क्रोधेन वै भद्र नष्टाश्चैव दिवौकसः ॥
1.100.m: the lord of great splendour, bowing down and supplicating, said to Bhadra: / "Enough of wrath, O Bhadra! The dwellers of heaven are indeed destroyed!

1.100.s:
prasīda kṣamyatāṃ sarvaṃ romajaiḥ saha suvrata
so 'pi bhadraḥ prabhāveṇa brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ //
1.100.d:
प्रसीद क्षम्यतां सर्वं रोमजैः सह सुव्रत
सो ऽपि भद्रः प्रभावेण ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ॥
1.100.m:
"Be gracious! O one of good vows, let everything be forgiven, along with those born of your hairs!"
And that Bhadra, through the power of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin,

1.100.s:
śamaṃ jagāma śanakaiḥ śāntastasthau tadājñayā
devo 'pi tatra bhagavān antarikṣe vṛṣadhvajaḥ //
1.100.d:
शमं जगाम शनकैः शान्तस्तस्थौ तदाज्ञया
देवो ऽपि तत्र भगवान् अन्तरिक्षे वृषध्वजः ॥
1.100.m:
gradually became calm, and being pacified, stood by his command.
The lord, the divine Vṛṣadhvaja, was also there in the sky,

1.100.s:
sagaṇaḥ sarvadaḥ śarvaḥ sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ
prārthitaścaiva devena brahmaṇā bhagavān bhavaḥ //
1.100.d:
सगणः सर्वदः शर्वः सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः
प्रार्थितश्चैव देवेन ब्रह्मणा भगवान् भवः ॥
1.100.m:
accompanied by his attendants, the all-bestower Śarva, Maheśvara of all the worlds.
And the divine Bhava was prayed to by the god Brahmā,

1.100.s:
hatānāṃ ca tadā teṣāṃ pradadau pūrvavattanum
indrasya ca śirastasya viṣṇoścaiva mahātmanaḥ //
1.100.d:
हतानां च तदा तेषां प्रददौ पूर्ववत्तनुम्
इन्द्रस्य च शिरस्तस्य विष्णोश्चैव महात्मनः ॥
1.100.m:
and then he gave to those who had been killed their bodies as before:
the head of Indra, and of the noble Viṣṇu,

1.100.s:
dakṣasya ca munīndrasya tathānyeṣāṃ maheśvaraḥ
vāgīśyāścaiva nāsāgraṃ devamātustathaiva ca //
1.100.d:
दक्षस्य च मुनीन्द्रस्य तथान्येषां महेश्वरः
वागीश्याश्चैव नासाग्रं देवमातुस्तथैव च ॥
1.100.m:
and of Dakṣa, chief of sages, and likewise of the others, Maheśvara [restored];
and the tip of the nose of Vāgīśī, as well as of the mother of the gods,

1.100.s:
naṣṭānāṃ jīvitaṃ caiva varāṇi vividhāni ca
dakṣasya dhvastavaktrasya śirasā bhagavānprabhuḥ //
1.100.d:
नष्टानां जीवितं चैव वराणि विविधानि च
दक्षस्य ध्वस्तवक्त्रस्य शिरसा भगवान्प्रभुः ॥
1.100.m:
and life to the destroyed, as well as various boons.
To Dakṣa whose face had been destroyed, the divine lord,

1.100.s:
kalpayāmāsa vai vaktraṃ līlayā ca mahān bhavaḥ
dakṣo 'pi labdhasaṃjñaś ca samutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ //
1.100.d:
कल्पयामास वै वक्त्रं लीलया च महान् भवः
दक्षो ऽपि लब्धसंज्ञश् च समुत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः ॥
1.100.m:
the great Bhava, playfully fashioned a face with a [goat's] head.
Dakṣa too, regaining consciousness, stood up with joined palms,

1.100.s:
tuṣṭāva devadeveśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam
stutastena mahātejāḥ pradāya vividhānvarān //
1.100.d:
तुष्टाव देवदेवेशं शङ्करं वृषभध्वजम्
स्तुतस्तेन महातेजाः प्रदाय विविधान्वरान् ॥
1.100.m:
and praised the god of the gods of gods, Śaṅkara Vṛṣabhadhvaja.
Praised by him, the one of great splendour bestowed various boons,

1.100.s:
gāṇapatyaṃ dadau tasmai dakṣāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe
devāś ca sarve deveśaṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ parameśvaram //
1.100.d:
गाणपत्यं ददौ तस्मै दक्षायाक्लिष्टकर्मणे
देवाश् च सर्वे देवेशं तुष्टुवुः परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.100.m:
and gave leadership of the gaṇas to that Dakṣa of unwearied deeds.
Then all the gods praised the lord of gods, Parameśvara,

1.100.s:
nārāyaṇaś ca bhagavān tuṣṭāva ca kṛtāñjaliḥ
brahmā ca munayaḥ sarve pṛthakpṛthagajodbhavam //
1.100.d:
नारायणश् च भगवान् तुष्टाव च कृताञ्जलिः
ब्रह्मा च मुनयः सर्वे पृथक्पृथगजोद्भवम् ॥
1.100.m:
and the divine Nārāyaṇa praised him with joined palms;
Brahmā and all the sages praised the one who sprang from the unborn, one by one,

1.100.s:
tuṣṭuvur devadeveśaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ vṛṣadhvajam
tān devān anugṛhyaiva bhavo 'pyantaradhīyata //
1.100.d:
तुष्टुवुर् देवदेवेशं नीलकण्ठं वृषध्वजम्
तान् देवान् अनुगृह्यैव भवो ऽप्यन्तरधीयत ॥
1.100.m:
they praised the god of the gods of gods, Nīlakaṇṭha Vṛṣadhvaja.
Having shown grace to those gods, Bhava disappeared.

1.101.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ himavataḥ putrī babhūvāṃbā satī śubhā
kathaṃ vā devadeveśam avāpa patimīśvaram //
1.101.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कथं हिमवतः पुत्री बभूवांबा सती शुभा
कथं वा देवदेवेशम् अवाप पतिमीश्वरम् ॥
1.101.m:
The sages said:
How did the auspicious Satī, the Mother, become the daughter of Himavat?
Or how did she obtain the lord, the god of the gods of gods, as her husband?

1.101.s:
sūta uvāca
sā menātanum āśritya svecchayaiva varāṅganā
tadā haimavatī jajñe tapasā ca dvijottamāḥ //
1.101.d:
सूत उवाच
सा मेनातनुम् आश्रित्य स्वेच्छयैव वराङ्गना
तदा हैमवती जज्ञे तपसा च द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.101.m:
Sūta said:
Resorting to the body of Menā by her own will, that excellent woman,
then, O best of the twice-born, through ascetic power was born as Haimavatī.

1.101.s:
jātakarmādikāḥ sarvāś cakāra ca girīśvaraḥ
dvādaśe ca tadā varṣe pūrṇe haimavatī śubhā //
1.101.d:
जातकर्मादिकाः सर्वाश् चकार च गिरीश्वरः
द्वादशे च तदा वर्षे पूर्णे हैमवती शुभा ॥
1.101.m:
The lord of mountains performed all the birth rites and others for her.
And then, when her twelfth year was completed, the auspicious Haimavatī

1.101.s:
tapastepe tayā sārdham anujā ca śubhānanā
anyā ca devī hyanujā sarvaloke namaskṛtā //
1.101.d:
तपस्तेपे तया सार्धम् अनुजा च शुभानना
अन्या च देवी ह्यनुजा सर्वलोके नमस्कृता ॥
1.101.m:
practised tapas, and with her her younger sister of fair face,
and another goddess, a younger sister bowed to in all worlds.

1.101.s:
ṛṣayaś ca tadā sarve sarvalokamaheśvarīm
tuṣṭuvus tapasā devīṃ samāvṛtya samantataḥ //
1.101.d:
ऋषयश् च तदा सर्वे सर्वलोकमहेश्वरीम्
तुष्टुवुस् तपसा देवीं समावृत्य समन्ततः ॥
1.101.m:
And then all the sages, surrounding the goddess Maheśvarī of all worlds on all sides,
praised her on account of her tapas.

1.101.s:
jyeṣṭhā hyaparṇā hyanujā caikaparṇā śubhānanā
tṛtīyā ca varārohā tathā caivaikapāṭalā //
1.101.d:
ज्येष्ठा ह्यपर्णा ह्यनुजा चैकपर्णा शुभानना
तृतीया च वरारोहा तथा चैवैकपाटला ॥
1.101.m:
The eldest was indeed Aparṇā, and the fair-faced younger sister was Ekaparṇā,
and the third, a woman of lovely hips, was Ekapāṭalā.

1.101.s:
tapasā ca mahādevyāḥ pārvatyāḥ parameśvaraḥ
vaśīkṛto mahādevaḥ sarvabhūtapatirbhavaḥ //
1.101.d:
तपसा च महादेव्याः पार्वत्याः परमेश्वरः
वशीकृतो महादेवः सर्वभूतपतिर्भवः ॥
1.101.m:
And by the tapas of the Mahādevī Pārvatī, Parameśvara,
Mahādeva Bhava, the lord of all beings, was won over.

1.101.s:
etasminneva kāle tu tārako nāma dānavaḥ
tārātmajo mahātejā babhūva ditinandanaḥ //
1.101.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु तारको नाम दानवः
तारात्मजो महातेजा बभूव दितिनन्दनः ॥
1.101.m:
At that very time, however, a dānava named Tāraka,
son of Tāra, of great splendour, was born, a son of Diti.

1.101.s:
tasya putrāstrayaścāpi tārakākṣo mahāsuraḥ
vidyunmālī ca bhagavān kamalākṣaś ca vīryavān //
1.101.d:
तस्य पुत्रास्त्रयश्चापि तारकाक्षो महासुरः
विद्युन्माली च भगवान् कमलाक्षश् च वीर्यवान् ॥
1.101.m:
He also had three sons: Tārakākṣa the great asura,
the divine Vidyunmālin, and the powerful Kamalākṣa.

1.101.s:
pitāmahas tathā caiṣāṃ tāro nāma mahābalaḥ
tapasā labdhavīryaś ca prasādādbrahmaṇaḥ prabhoḥ //
1.101.d:
पितामहस् तथा चैषां तारो नाम महाबलः
तपसा लब्धवीर्यश् च प्रसादाद्ब्रह्मणः प्रभोः ॥
1.101.m:
And their grandfather was Tāra, of great strength,
who had gained strength through tapas by the grace of the lord Brahmā.

1.101.s:
so 'pi tāro mahātejās trailokyaṃ sacarācaram
vijitya samare pūrvaṃ viṣṇuṃ ca jitavān asau //
1.101.d:
सो ऽपि तारो महातेजास् त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम्
विजित्य समरे पूर्वं विष्णुं च जितवान् असौ ॥
1.101.m:
That Tāra, too, of great splendour, having previously conquered the three worlds
with their moving and unmoving beings in battle, conquered Viṣṇu.

1.101.s:
tayoḥ samabhavadyuddhaṃ sughoraṃ romaharṣaṇam
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu divārātram aviśramam //
1.101.d:
तयोः समभवद्युद्धं सुघोरं रोमहर्षणम्
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं तु दिवारात्रम् अविश्रमम् ॥
1.101.m:
Between the two there occurred a battle, terrible and hair-raising,
for a thousand divine years, day and night without rest.

1.101.s:
sarathaṃ viṣṇumādāya cikṣepa śatayojanam
tāreṇa vijitaḥ saṃkhye dudrāva garuḍadhvajaḥ //
1.101.d:
सरथं विष्णुमादाय चिक्षेप शतयोजनम्
तारेण विजितः संख्ये दुद्राव गरुडध्वजः ॥
1.101.m:
Taking Viṣṇu along with his chariot, he hurled him a hundred yojanas.
Defeated in battle by Tāra, Garuḍadhvaja fled.

1.101.s:
tāro varāñchataguṇaṃ labdhvā śataguṇaṃ balam
pitāmahājjagatsarvam avāpa ditinandanaḥ //
1.101.d:
तारो वराञ्छतगुणं लब्ध्वा शतगुणं बलम्
पितामहाज्जगत्सर्वम् अवाप दितिनन्दनः ॥
1.101.m:
Having obtained a hundredfold boons and a hundredfold strength
from Pitāmaha, Tāra, that son of Diti, took the entire world.

1.101.s:
devendrapramukhāñjitvā devāndeveśvareśvaraḥ
vārayāmāsa tair devān sarvalokeṣu māyayā //
1.101.d:
देवेन्द्रप्रमुखाञ्जित्वा देवान्देवेश्वरेश्वरः
वारयामास तैर् देवान् सर्वलोकेषु मायया ॥
1.101.m:
Having conquered the gods headed by Devendra, the master of the lords of gods
drove away the gods in all worlds by means of them, through illusion.

1.101.s:
devatāś ca sahendreṇa tārakādbhayapīḍitāḥ
na śāntiṃ lebhire śūrāḥ śaraṇaṃ vā bhayārditāḥ //
1.101.d:
देवताश् च सहेन्द्रेण तारकाद्भयपीडिताः
न शान्तिं लेभिरे शूराः शरणं वा भयार्दिताः ॥
1.101.m:
And the deities along with Indra, afflicted with fear of Tāraka,
though heroic, found neither peace nor shelter, tormented with fear.

1.101.s:
tadāmarapatiḥ śrīmān saṃnipatyāmaraprabhuḥ
uvācāṅgirasaṃ devo devānāmapi saṃnidhau //
1.101.d:
तदामरपतिः श्रीमान् संनिपत्यामरप्रभुः
उवाचाङ्गिरसं देवो देवानामपि संनिधौ ॥
1.101.m:
Then the illustrious lord of immortals, the chief of the immortals, assembling,
that god spoke to the descendant of Aṅgiras, in the presence of the gods:

1.101.s:
bhagavaṃstārako nāma tārajo dānavottamaḥ
tena saṃnihatā yuddhe vatsā gopatinā yathā //
1.101.d:
भगवंस्तारको नाम तारजो दानवोत्तमः
तेन संनिहता युद्धे वत्सा गोपतिना यथा ॥
1.101.m:
"O venerable one, an excellent dānava named Tāraka, the son of Tāra,
has struck down [our forces] in battle, like calves by a bull.

1.101.s:
bhayāttasmānmahābhāga bṛhadyuddhe bṛhaspate
aniketā bhramantyete śakuntā iva pañjare //
1.101.d:
भयात्तस्मान्महाभाग बृहद्युद्धे बृहस्पते
अनिकेता भ्रमन्त्येते शकुन्ता इव पञ्जरे ॥
1.101.m:
Out of fear of him, O noble Bṛhaspati, in this great battle,
these wander homeless, like birds in a cage.

1.101.s:
asmākaṃ yāny amoghāni āyudhāny aṅgiro vara
tāni moghāni jāyante prabhāvādamaradviṣaḥ //
1.101.d:
अस्माकं यान्य् अमोघानि आयुधान्य् अङ्गिरो वर
तानि मोघानि जायन्ते प्रभावादमरद्विषः ॥
1.101.m:
Our weapons that were never failing, O best descendant of Aṅgiras,
they are rendered futile by the power of the enemy of the immortals.

1.101.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi dviguṇāni bṛhaspate
viṣṇunā yodhito yuddhe tenāpi na ca sūditaḥ //
1.101.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि द्विगुणानि बृहस्पते
विष्णुना योधितो युद्धे तेनापि न च सूदितः ॥
1.101.m:
For twice ten thousand years, O Bṛhaspati,
he was fought in battle by Viṣṇu, yet was not slain even by him.

1.101.s:
yastenānirjito yuddhe viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
kathamasmadvidhastasya sthāsyate samare 'grataḥ //
1.101.d:
यस्तेनानिर्जितो युद्धे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना
कथमस्मद्विधस्तस्य स्थास्यते समरे ऽग्रतः ॥
1.101.m:
If he was not overcome in battle by the mighty Viṣṇu,
how can one like us stand before him in combat?"

1.101.s:
evam uktas tu śakreṇa jīvaḥ sārdhaṃ surādhipaiḥ
sahasrākṣeṇa ca vibhuṃ samprāpyāha kuśadhvajam //
1.101.d:
एवम् उक्तस् तु शक्रेण जीवः सार्धं सुराधिपैः
सहस्राक्षेण च विभुं सम्प्राप्याह कुशध्वजम् ॥
1.101.m:
Thus addressed by Śakra, Jīva, together with the chiefs of the gods
and with the Thousand-Eyed, approached the all-pervading Kuśadhvaja and said [so].

1.101.s:
so 'pi tasya mukhācchrutvā praṇayātpraṇatārtihā
devairaśeṣaiḥ sendraistu jīvamāha pitāmahaḥ //
1.101.d:
सो ऽपि तस्य मुखाच्छ्रुत्वा प्रणयात्प्रणतार्तिहा
देवैरशेषैः सेन्द्रैस्तु जीवमाह पितामहः ॥
1.101.m:
Hearing this from his mouth with affection, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow,
Pitāmaha, together with all the gods and Indra, said to Jīva:

1.101.s:
jāne vo 'rtiṃ surendrāṇāṃ tathāpi śṛṇu sāṃpratam
vinindya dakṣaṃ yā devī satī rudrāṅgasaṃbhavā //
1.101.d:
जाने वो ऽर्तिं सुरेन्द्राणां तथापि शृणु सांप्रतम्
विनिन्द्य दक्षं या देवी सती रुद्राङ्गसंभवा ॥
1.101.m:
"I know the distress of you lords of gods; nevertheless, listen now.
The goddess who, having reproached Dakṣa, was Satī born of Rudra's body,

1.101.s:
umā haimavatī jajñe sarvalokanamaskṛtā
tasyāścaiveha rūpeṇa yūyaṃ devāḥ surottamāḥ //
1.101.d:
उमा हैमवती जज्ञे सर्वलोकनमस्कृता
तस्याश्चैवेह रूपेण यूयं देवाः सुरोत्तमाः ॥
1.101.m:
was born as Umā Haimavatī, bowed to by all the worlds.
And by her beauty here, O gods, best of immortals,

1.101.s:
vibhoryatadhvamākraṣṭuṃ rudrasyāsya mano mahat
tayoryogena sambhūtaḥ skandaḥ śaktidharaḥ prabhuḥ //
1.101.d:
विभोर्यतध्वमाक्रष्टुं रुद्रस्यास्य मनो महत्
तयोर्योगेन सम्भूतः स्कन्दः शक्तिधरः प्रभुः ॥
1.101.m:
strive to draw the great mind of this all-pervading Rudra.
Born from their union, the lord Skanda, bearer of the spear,

1.101.s:
ṣaḍāsyo dvādaśabhujaḥ senānīḥ pāvakiḥ prabhuḥ
svāheyaḥ kārtikeyaś ca gāṅgeyaḥ śaradhāmajaḥ //
1.101.d:
षडास्यो द्वादशभुजः सेनानीः पावकिः प्रभुः
स्वाहेयः कार्तिकेयश् च गाङ्गेयः शरधामजः ॥
1.101.m:
six-faced, twelve-armed, commander of the army, son of Pāvaka, the lord,
son of Svāhā, Kārtikeya, son of Gaṅgā, born in the reed-thicket,

1.101.s:
devaḥ śākho viśākhaś ca naigameśaś ca vīryavān
senāpatiḥ kumārākhyaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ //
1.101.d:
देवः शाखो विशाखश् च नैगमेशश् च वीर्यवान्
सेनापतिः कुमाराख्यः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः ॥
1.101.m:
the divine Śākha, Viśākha, and the powerful Naigameśa,
the commander of the army known as Kumāra, bowed to by all the worlds,

1.101.s:
līlayaiva mahāsenaḥ prabalaṃ tārakāsuram
bālo 'pi vinihatyaiko devān saṃtārayiṣyati //
1.101.d:
लीलयैव महासेनः प्रबलं तारकासुरम्
बालो ऽपि विनिहत्यैको देवान् संतारयिष्यति ॥
1.101.m:
that Mahāsena, even as a boy, having slain the mighty Tārakāsura
playfully, all alone, will deliver the gods."

1.101.s:
evam uktas tadā tena brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā
bṛhaspatis tathā sendrair devair devaṃ praṇamya tam //
1.101.d:
एवम् उक्तस् तदा तेन ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना
बृहस्पतिस् तथा सेन्द्रैर् देवैर् देवं प्रणम्य तम् ॥
1.101.m:
Thus addressed then by that Brahmā Parameṣṭhin,
Bṛhaspati, having bowed to that god along with the gods and Indra,

1.101.s:
meroḥ śikharamāsādya smaraṃ sasmāra suvrataḥ
smaraṇāddevadevasya smaro 'pi saha bhāryayā //
1.101.d:
मेरोः शिखरमासाद्य स्मरं सस्मार सुव्रतः
स्मरणाद्देवदेवस्य स्मरो ऽपि सह भार्यया ॥
1.101.m:
reached the summit of Meru, and, faithful to his vow, remembered Smara.
By the remembrance of the god of gods, Smara also, along with his wife,

1.101.s:
ratyā samaṃ samāgamya namaskṛtya kṛtāñjaliḥ
saśakramāha taṃ jīvaṃ jagajjīvo dvijottamāḥ //
1.101.d:
